ex.az: VGA/HDMI 是接顯示器的，鍵盤用 USB。

ex.q: State one advantage of an integrated sound card over a dedicated sound card.
ex.a: Lower cost: it replaces a separate interface card, which is usually more expensive, lowering the cost of building the computer (Checkpoint 2.1 Q2, answer C).
ex.az: 內置音效卡成本較低。

cards.en:
A central processing unit (CPU) is a processor that consists of many chips to process data and instructions. It controls most of the operations performed by a computer, so it is considered the 'brain' of a computer.
A CPU generates a large amount of heat as a by-product, so it usually needs cooling fans or heat sinks to prevent overheating. In the system unit photo, the processor sits under the fan.
The CPU and GPU usually have the highest energy consumption among components in a system unit (useful when choosing a PSU).
cards.zh:
CPU（中央處理器）由多個晶片組成，負責處理資料和指令（process data and instructions），並控制電腦大部分運作，所以被稱為電腦的「大腦（brain）」。
CPU 運作時會產生大量熱，需要散熱風扇或散熱片（cooling fans / heat sinks）防止過熱。主機圖中處理器就在風扇下面。
CPU 和 GPU 通常是主機內耗電最高的組件，選 PSU 時要考慮。

ex.q: Why does a CPU need a heat sink or cooling fan?
ex.a: A CPU generates a large amount of heat as a by-product when it operates. The fan/heat sink dissipates the heat and prevents the CPU from overheating.
ex.az: CPU 運作產生大量熱，需要散熱防止過熱。

cards.tz: GPU 與 CPU 的分別
cards.en:
A graphics processing unit (GPU) is also a processor that processes data and executes commands. Differences:
  • A GPU is more specialised in graphic rendering, while a CPU is made to handle various types of tasks.
  • A GPU has more cores and is thus more capable of multitasking (many simple computations at the same time).
With a GPU doing graphics processing, the computing power of the CPU is freed up for other tasks. A GPU also needs cooling fans or heat sinks. A GPU appears either in a dedicated graphics card or as an integrated GPU (iGPU).
Application: GPUs are the core for training artificial intelligence / deep learning, because AI must analyse large amounts of data quickly and GPUs are good at doing a lot of simple computing at the same time, while CPUs are good at complex tasks.
Note: a CPU can process graphics, just usually not as well as a GPU.
cards.zh:
GPU（圖形處理器）也是處理器。分別：
  • GPU 專門做圖形渲染（graphic rendering）；CPU 處理各種不同工作。
  • GPU 核心較多，所以更擅長同時處理大量簡單運算（multitasking）。
GPU 負責圖形後，CPU 的運算能力可以騰出來做其他工作。GPU 也需要散熱。GPU 可以是獨立顯示卡或 iGPU。
應用：人工智能（深度學習）以 GPU 為核心，因為要同時分析大量數據，GPU 擅長大量簡單平行運算；CPU 擅長複雜任務。
注意：CPU 也能處理圖形，只是通常不及 GPU。

ex.q: Which is correct? A. A CPU cannot process graphics while a GPU can. B. A CPU has a cooling fan while a GPU does not. C. A GPU always contains RAM while a CPU does not. D. A GPU can be integrated into a CPU.
ex.a: A: CPU can process graphics. B: both can have fans. C: an iGPU has no dedicated RAM. D: an iGPU is a GPU integrated into a CPU. Answer: D (Textbook Example 2.1 Q2).
ex.az: iGPU 就是整合到 CPU 的 GPU，答案 D。

cards.en:
A graphics card (display card / video card) contains a GPU plus:
  • RAM used only for graphics processing (separate from system RAM);
  • a digital-to-analog converter that converts processing results into analog signals for display units such as monitors or projectors.
An integrated graphics processing unit (iGPU) is a GPU integrated into the chipset of a motherboard or a CPU.
TypeAdvantagesSuitable for
Graphics cardHigher graphics processing powerComputer aided design, video editing, gaming
iGPULower cost; lower energy consumptionGeneral word processing
Disadvantage of iGPU: lower graphics processing power.
cards.zh:
Graphics card（顯示卡 / 圖形卡）包含 GPU 以及：
  • 只用於圖形處理的 RAM（顯示記憶體，和系統 RAM 分開）；
  • Digital-to-analog converter（數碼至模擬轉換器）：把結果轉成模擬訊號給顯示器/投影機。
iGPU 是整合在主機板晶片組或 CPU 的 GPU。
顯示卡：圖形處理能力高，適合 CAD、影片剪接、遊戲。iGPU：成本低、耗電低，但圖形處理能力較低，適合一般文書處理。

ex.q: A secretary only does word processing; a student does 3D animation. Recommend graphics card or iGPU for each.
ex.a: Secretary: iGPU, because of lower cost and lower energy consumption, and word processing needs little graphics power. Student: dedicated graphics card, because 3D animation needs higher graphics processing power.
ex.az: 文書處理用 iGPU（平、省電）；3D 動畫用顯示卡（圖形能力高）。

cards.t: Storage device overview: main memory vs secondary storage
cards.tz: 儲存設備概覽：主記憶體 vs 輔助儲存器
cards.en:
Main memory (primary storage) refers to ROM and RAM.
TypeVolatilityRewritabilityUsage
RAMVolatileCan be rewritten at high speedStores data temporarily for processing
ROMNon-volatileUsually cannot be rewrittenStores firmware required to start a computer
Volatile: data disappears once the computer shuts down. Non-volatile: data persists after shutdown.
Secondary storage is always non-volatile, because it stores data for future use. Types differ in storage size, data transfer rate and lifespan; examples: hard disk, SSD, USB flash drive.
cards.zh:
Main memory（主記憶體）= primary storage，包括 RAM 和 ROM。
RAM：volatile（易失性），可高速改寫，暫時儲存待處理的資料。ROM：non-volatile（非易失性），通常不能改寫，儲存開機用的 firmware（韌體）。
Volatile = 關機後資料消失；Non-volatile = 關機後資料仍在。
Secondary storage（輔助儲存器）全部都是 non-volatile，用來儲存資料供日後使用。不同種類的容量、傳輸速度和壽命不同，例如 hard disk、SSD、USB flash drive。

ex.q: Which statement about volatile memory is correct? A. Data remains after shutdown. B. Data disappears once the computer shuts down. C. Data will not be processed. D. It stores the system firmware.
ex.a: Volatile means data is lost when power is off. Firmware is in ROM (non-volatile). Answer: B (Chapter Exercise MC 11).
ex.az: Volatile = 關機資料消失，答案 B。

cards.en:
A power supply unit (PSU) converts high-voltage alternating current (AC) to low-voltage direct current (DC), which provides suitable power for the computer to operate. Like a CPU, a PSU needs cooling fans or heat sinks.
PSUs come in different powers, measured in watts (W). Before assembling a computer, assess the energy consumption of its components to select a suitable PSU. Tip: the CPU and GPU usually consume the most energy.
cards.zh:
PSU（電源供應器）把高電壓交流電（AC）轉換成低電壓直流電（DC），為電腦提供合適電源。PSU 也需要風扇/散熱片。
PSU 功率以瓦特（W）計。砌機前要評估各組件的耗電量，再選合適 PSU。提示：CPU 和 GPU 通常最耗電。

ex.q: A PC has a CPU rated 125 W, a GPU 220 W and other parts about 100 W. Should a 400 W PSU be chosen?
ex.a: Total ≈ 125 + 220 + 100 = 445 W > 400 W, so a 400 W PSU is not enough. Choose a PSU with a higher power (e.g. 550 W or more) to leave a margin.
ex.az: 總耗電約 445 W，大過 400 W，要選更大功率的 PSU。

cards.en:
A computer connects every component by transferring data and control signals using buses. Some buses connect internal components (e.g. CPU and main memory) inside the system unit; others connect the system unit with external components such as input and output devices. Analogy: the highway is the bus, vehicles are the data/signals.
A system bus transfers data and control signals between processors and various components. The amount of data a bus can transfer at a time is the bus width; the bus width is usually the same as the word length of the CPU.
The system bus has three parts: control bus, address bus and data bus.
cards.zh:
電腦用匯流排（bus）傳送資料和控制訊號來連接各組件。有些連接主機內部組件（如 CPU 和主記憶體），有些連接主機與外部輸入/輸出設備。比喻：公路 = bus，車輛 = 資料/訊號。
System bus（系統匯流排）在處理器和各組件之間傳送資料和控制訊號。一次可傳送的資料量叫 bus width（匯流排寬度），通常等於 CPU 的 word length。
系統匯流排分三種：control bus、address bus、data bus。

ex.q: A CPU has a word length of 64 bits. What is the likely bus width, and how many bytes can be transferred at a time?
ex.a: Bus width is usually equal to word length: 64 bits = 64 ÷ 8 = 8 bytes per transfer.
ex.az: bus width 通常 = word length = 64 bits = 8 bytes。

cards.t: Control bus, address bus and data bus
cards.en:
TypeObject to transferDirection
Control busControl signalsOne-way: from processors to components
Address busMemory addressesOne-way: from processors to components
Data busData or instructionsTwo-way: between processors and components
  • Control bus carries control signals to storage, input and output devices and ensures the correct timing of data transfer. Signals are sent from, but not received by, processors.
  • Address bus carries memory addresses that indicate which data to fetch or store.
  • Data bus: data is both sent from and received by processors.
Exam trap: statements with the right object but wrong direction (e.g. 'address bus transfers addresses from components to processors') are wrong.
cards.zh:
Control bus（控制匯流排）：傳送控制訊號，單向（處理器→組件），確保資料傳送時間正確。
Address bus（位址匯流排）：傳送記憶體位址，單向（處理器→組件），指明要讀取或儲存哪個資料。
Data bus（數據匯流排）：傳送資料或指令，雙向（處理器↔組件）。
陷阱：傳送內容對但方向錯的句子是錯的，例如「address bus 由組件傳位址到處理器」✗；「data bus 只由處理器傳到組件」✗。

ex.q: Which is/are correct? (1) An SSD can be connected through SATA bus. (2) An address bus transfers memory addresses from components to processors. (3) A data bus transfers data only from processors to components.
ex.a: (1) correct: SATA connects secondary storage. (2) wrong direction: processors → components. (3) wrong: data bus is two-way. Answer: (1) only (Textbook Example 2.1 Q3).

cards.tz: SATA 與 PCIe 匯流排（增潤）
cards.en:
Serial advanced technology attachment bus (SATA bus) connects secondary storage devices such as hard disks, solid-state drives (SSD) and optical disc drives (ODD) to computers.
Peripheral component interconnect express bus (PCIe bus) is mainly used for connecting graphics cards, sound cards and network interface cards (NIC). It allows processors and other components to transfer data at a high speed.
Note: USB and PCIe are not part of the 'system bus' trio (control/address/data), so in 'which bus transfers control signals' the answer is the control bus.
cards.zh:
SATA bus：連接輔助儲存器，例如 hard disk、SSD、光碟機（ODD）。
PCIe bus：主要連接顯示卡、音效卡、網卡（NIC），讓處理器和組件高速傳送資料。
注意：USB、PCIe 不是系統匯流排三種（control/address/data）之一；問「哪種系統匯流排傳送控制訊號」答 control bus。

ex.q: Which system bus transfers control signals from processors to components? A. USB B. Data bus C. Control bus D. PCIe bus
ex.a: Answer: C (Textbook Checkpoint 2.1 Q3).
ex.az: 控制訊號由 control bus 傳送。

cards.en:
Universal serial bus (USB) is commonly used to connect external devices: keyboards, mice, printers, webcams, image scanners, external storage. Motherboards usually have multiple USB ports.
USB supports hot swapping: users can plug or swap devices while the computer system is still operating.
Connector standards: USB-A (flash drives, most PC ports), USB-B micro (older phones), USB-C (reversible, newer devices).
Versions can be told apart by plug colour: USB 1.0 white, USB 2.0 black, USB 3.0 blue. USB 3.0 is increasingly popular due to its higher data transfer rate.
Uses of a USB port include connecting a keyboard, storing data in a flash drive, installing an OS from a flash drive; defragmentation of a hard disk is not a USB usage.
cards.zh:
USB 常用來接外置設備：鍵盤、滑鼠、打印機、網絡攝影機、掃描器、外置儲存器。主機板通常有多個 USB 埠。
USB 支援 hot swapping（熱插拔）：電腦運作中可以插入或更換設備。
接頭：USB-A、USB-B micro、USB-C。
版本顏色：USB 1.0 白色、USB 2.0 黑色、USB 3.0 藍色；USB 3.0 因傳輸速度較高越來越普及。
USB 用途：接鍵盤、用 USB 手指存資料、用 USB 手指安裝作業系統；硬碟重組（fragmentation）不是 USB 用途。

ex.q: Which is not a usage of a USB port? A. Connecting a keyboard B. Storing data in a flash drive C. Fragmentation of hard disk D. Installing OS from a flash drive
ex.a: Defragmenting a hard disk is a utility task, not a port usage. Answer: C (Chapter Exercise MC 8).
ex.az: 答案 C。

ex.q: A USB plug has a blue tongue. Which version is it and why might it be preferred?
ex.a: Blue = USB 3.0, preferred for its higher data transfer rate.
ex.az: 藍色 = USB 3.0，傳輸較快。

cards.t: CPU components: CU, ALU and registers
cards.en:
A CPU is the main processor, responsible for data processing. Two main components: the Control Unit (CU) and the Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU). Processing also involves registers, memory that can be quickly accessed by the CPU.
ALU performs:
  • arithmetic operations: +, −, ×, ÷;
  • logical operations: comparison (=, ≠, <, >, ≤, ≥), conjunction (AND), disjunction (OR), negation (NOT).
The result is transferred to a register called the accumulator via the data bus.
CU controls: the response of the ALU and other devices to instructions, and the data flow between the CPU, other components and devices. The CU decodes instructions; the ALU executes them. (The CU does not perform logical operations; that is the ALU.)
Analogy: CU = teacher guiding, ALU = student doing homework, registers = the homework.
cards.zh:
CPU 是主處理器，負責資料處理，主要由 Control Unit (CU) 控制部件和 Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU) 算術及邏輯運算部件組成，並用到暫存器（registers）。
ALU 做算術運算（+ − × ÷）和邏輯運算（比較 = ≠ < > ≤ ≥、AND、OR、NOT），結果經 data bus 送到 accumulator（累加器）。
CU 控制 ALU 及其他設備對指令的反應，以及 CPU 與其他組件/設備之間的資料流。CU 負責解碼（decode），ALU 負責執行（execute）。CU 不做邏輯運算。
比喻：CU = 老師指導，ALU = 學生做功課，暫存器 = 功課本身。

ex.q: Classify: (i) checking whether x ≥ 18; (ii) computing price × 0.9; (iii) deciding the order in which data moves between RAM and the CPU.
ex.a: (i) comparison: ALU (logical operation). (ii) multiplication: ALU (arithmetic). (iii) controlling data flow: CU.
ex.az: 比較和乘法都是 ALU；控制資料流是 CU。

ex.q: Which CPU component decodes an instruction during a machine cycle?
ex.a: Control Unit (CU) (Checkpoint 2.2 Q1, answer C).
ex.az: CU 解碼。

cards.t: Registers: CIR, PC, MAR, MDR, accumulator
cards.en:
Registers are memory accessed by the CPU at high speed. A CPU has a limited number of registers, each small (usually 32 or 64 bits, depending on the OS and word length). They temporarily store data needed during processing.
RegisterStores
Current instruction register (CIR)the instruction currently being executed
Program counter (PC)the address of the next instruction to be executed; after its address is fetched, the PC is updated to the address of the instruction after next
Memory address register (MAR)the memory address to be read from or written into; connected to main memory through the address bus
Memory data register (MDR)the data read from / to be written into the address in MAR; connected through the data bus
Accumulatorthe arithmetic operation result from the ALU
Registers that hold addresses: PC and MAR. Registers that hold data/instructions: MDR, CIR, accumulator.
cards.zh:
Registers（暫存器）是 CPU 可以高速存取的記憶體，數量有限，每個很小（通常 32 或 64 bits）。
CIR 現行指令寄存器：存放正在執行的指令。
PC 程式計數器：存放下一個指令的位址；位址被取走後更新為再下一個。
MAR 記憶體位址寄存器：存放要讀/寫的記憶體位址，經 address bus 連主記憶體。
MDR 記憶體數據寄存器：存放從 MAR 位址讀出或要寫入的資料，經 data bus 連主記憶體。
Accumulator 累加器：存放 ALU 的運算結果。
存位址的：PC、MAR；存資料/指令的：MDR、CIR、accumulator。

ex.q: Which store memory addresses in a machine cycle? (1) PC (2) MAR (3) RAM (4) CIR
ex.a: PC stores the address of the next instruction; MAR stores the address of the instruction. RAM stores data; CIR stores instruction. Answer: (1) and (2) only (Textbook Example 2.2 Q1).
ex.az: PC 和 MAR 存位址。

ex.q: Which statement is correct? A. PC stores the address of the next instruction. B. MAR stores the data read from memory. C. Accumulator stores the current instruction. D. CU performs logical operations.
ex.a: B describes MDR, C describes CIR, D describes ALU. Answer: A (Chapter Exercise MC 6).
ex.az: 答案 A。

cards.en:
The performance of a CPU is greatly affected by its cache memory. Like RAM, cache memory is volatile. However, the access rate of the cache in the CPU is higher than that of RAM. It facilitates data access from main memory by temporarily storing the data or instructions that are expected to be accessed most frequently.
Relationship: CPU ↔ cache memory ↔ main memory ↔ secondary storage (the CPU can also access main memory directly). The CPU never reads secondary storage directly; data must first be loaded into main memory.
Speed order: register > cache > RAM > SSD > hard disk > magnetic tape.
cards.zh:
CPU 的表現受 cache memory（快取記憶體）影響很大。Cache 和 RAM 一樣是 volatile，但存取速度比 RAM 快。它暫時存放預計最常用的資料或指令，加快從主記憶體存取資料。
關係：CPU ↔ cache ↔ 主記憶體 ↔ 輔助儲存器（CPU 也可直接存取主記憶體）。CPU 不會直接讀輔助儲存器，要先載入主記憶體。
速度：register > cache > RAM > SSD > hard disk > magnetic tape。

ex.q: Arrange in descending order of data access rate: (1) cache memory (2) flash memory (3) register
ex.a: Register is fastest, then cache, then flash memory (SSD). (3) > (1) > (2) (Checkpoint 2.4 Q1, answer C).
ex.az: 暫存器 > 快取 > 快閃記憶體。

cards.en:
Most computers are based on the von Neumann architecture, featuring a machine cycle (also called instruction cycle) with four phases: fetching, decoding, executing and storing.
  • Fetch: the instruction is fetched from RAM to the CPU.
  • Decode: the CU decodes it.
  • Execute: the ALU executes it.
  • Store: the result is stored (accumulator, and back to RAM).
The diagram is a triangle: RAM —fetch→ CU (decode) → ALU (execute) —store→ RAM.
After the last step the cycle returns to the start if there is another instruction. 'Fetching instructions from MAR' is wrong wording: instructions are fetched from main memory; MAR only holds the address.
cards.zh:
大部分電腦基於 von Neumann architecture（馮紐曼架構），有機器周期（machine cycle / instruction cycle）四個階段：fetching（擷取）、decoding（解碼）、executing（執行）、storing（儲存）。
Fetch：從 RAM 擷取指令；Decode：CU 解碼；Execute：ALU 執行；Store：儲存結果。
圖：RAM →fetch→ CU（decode）→ ALU（execute）→store→ RAM。
完成後如仍有指令就重新開始。「從 MAR 擷取指令」是錯的說法：指令從主記憶體擷取，MAR 只存位址。

ex.q: Which is not involved in a machine cycle? A. Updating the address stored in the PC B. Fetching instructions from MAR C. Decoding instructions D. Executing instructions
ex.a: Instructions are fetched from main memory, not from MAR (MAR holds the address only). Answer: B (Chapter Exercise MC 7).
ex.az: 指令不是從 MAR 擷取，答案 B。

cards.t: The seven steps of the machine cycle
cards.en:
StepPhaseDescription
1FetchThe memory address stored in the PC is fetched to the MAR.
2FetchThe PC is updated with the address of the instruction after next.
3FetchThe address in the MAR is transferred to main memory via the address bus.
4FetchThe instruction/data at that address is transferred from main memory to the MDR via the data bus.
5FetchThe instruction/data in the MDR is copied to the CIR.
6Decode and executeThe instruction in the CIR is decoded by the CU and then executed by the ALU.
7StoreThe processing result is stored in the accumulator.
Flow to memorise: PC → MAR → (address bus) → main memory → (data bus) → MDR → CIR → CU → ALU → accumulator. After step 7, return to step 1 if there is an instruction to execute.
cards.zh:
七步驟：
1 (Fetch) PC 的位址送到 MAR。
2 (Fetch) PC 更新為下一個指令的位址。
3 (Fetch) MAR 的位址經 address bus 送到主記憶體。
4 (Fetch) 該位址的指令/資料經 data bus 由主記憶體送到 MDR。
5 (Fetch) MDR 內容複製到 CIR。
6 (Decode and execute) CIR 的指令由 CU 解碼，再由 ALU 執行。
7 (Store) 結果存入 accumulator。
口訣：PC → MAR → 位址匯流排 → 主記憶體 → 數據匯流排 → MDR → CIR → CU → ALU → 累加器。完成後如有指令回到步驟 1。

ex.q: State, in order, the registers and buses that an instruction passes through from the PC until it reaches the CU.
ex.a: 1. Address from PC to MAR; 2. PC incremented; 3. MAR sends the address to main memory via the address bus; 4. instruction returns to MDR via the data bus; 5. MDR copies it to CIR; 6. CU decodes the instruction in the CIR.
ex.az: PC→MAR→address bus→主記憶體→data bus→MDR→CIR→CU。

ex.q: In which step is the data bus used, and why is the address bus not used in that step?
ex.a: Step 4: the instruction (data) travels from main memory to the MDR, which needs the two-way data bus. The address bus is one-way (processor to memory) and only carries addresses (used in step 3).
ex.az: 第 4 步用 data bus 傳送指令；address bus 只在第 3 步傳位址。

cards.t: Visualising register contents in the machine cycle
cards.tz: 機器周期中暫存器內容的變化
cards.en:
Textbook Table 2.10 tracks each register through stages 0–7:
StageCIRPCMARMDREvent
0addr of instructionstart
1addr of instructionaddr of instructionPC copied to MAR
2addr of nextaddrPC updated
3nextaddrmemory receives address
4nextaddrinstructionmemory transfers instruction
5instructionnextaddrinstructioncopied to CIR
6instructionnextaddrinstructionCU decodes, ALU executes
7instructionnextaddrinstructionALU transfers result to accumulator
Key observation: from stage 2 onwards the PC already points to the next instruction while the current one is still being processed.
cards.zh:
課本表 2.10 顯示各暫存器在 0–7 階段的內容：
階段 1：PC 的位址複製到 MAR。階段 2：PC 更新為下一個指令位址。階段 3：主記憶體收到位址。階段 4：指令送到 MDR。階段 5：指令複製到 CIR。階段 6：CU 解碼、ALU 執行。階段 7：結果送到 accumulator。
重點：由第 2 階段開始，PC 已經指向下一個指令，而目前的指令仍在處理中。考試可能問某一階段某暫存器的內容。

ex.q: Instructions are at addresses 100, 101, 102. The CPU starts executing the instruction at 100. After step 5, what do the PC, MAR and CIR contain?
ex.a: Step 1: MAR = 100. Step 2: PC = 101. Step 4: MDR = instruction at 100. Step 5: CIR = instruction at 100. So PC = 101, MAR = 100, CIR = instruction at address 100.
ex.az: PC=101，MAR=100，CIR=位址 100 的指令。

cards.en:
The timing of fetching, decoding, executing and storing is controlled by the CPU clock. A CPU can only execute a certain number of instructions per clock cycle, so the duration of a clock cycle is an important performance factor. Clock rate = the number of clock cycles a CPU performs in one second.
Clock rateValueClock cycleValue
Hz1 per secondms10−3 s
kHz103µs10−6 s
MHz106ns10−9 s
GHz109ps10−12 s
Clock cycle time = 1 ÷ clock rate. A higher clock rate usually means better performance but higher energy consumption. The relationship with overall performance is not linearly proportional: e.g. if RAM and hard disk clock rates are much lower than the CPU's, the CPU is starved for data and cannot process faster.
cards.zh:
Fetch、decode、execute、store 的時間由 CPU 的時鐘（clock）控制。Clock rate（時鐘頻率）= 每秒的時鐘周期數。
單位：Hz（每秒 1 次）、kHz（10³）、MHz（10⁶）、GHz（10⁹）。周期時間單位：ms（10⁻³ s）、µs（10⁻⁶）、ns（10⁻⁹）、ps（10⁻¹²）。
時鐘周期 = 1 ÷ 時鐘頻率。
時鐘頻率越高通常效能越好，但耗電越高；兩者關係不是線性正比（not linearly proportional）：如 RAM、硬碟太慢，CPU 會「starved for data」（等資料），快不起來。

ex.q: A CPU runs at 2.5 GHz. Find the length of one clock cycle in ns.
ex.a: Clock cycle = 1 ÷ (2.5 × 109) s = 4 × 10−10 s = 0.4 ns.

ex.q: A clock cycle lasts 250 ps. What is the clock rate?

cards.en:
A core is an individual processor unit inside a CPU. The number of cores determines the number of processes that can be run at the same time.
A CPU with more cores usually performs better than one with fewer cores in the case of multitasking. However, the relationship between number of cores and overall processing speed is not linearly proportional.
Analogy: an exam question with parts (a)–(d) where (b) needs the answer of (a): assigning more people does not necessarily solve it faster, because some work must be done in sequence.
cards.zh:
Core（核心）是 CPU 內獨立的處理單元。核心數目決定可同時執行的程序（process）數目。
多核心的 CPU 在多工（multitasking）時通常表現較好，但核心數與整體速度不成線性正比。
比喻：一題考試題分 (a)(b)(c)(d)，(b) 要用 (a) 的答案，多人一起做不一定更快，因為部分工作必須按次序完成。所以 8 核不一定是 4 核的兩倍快。

ex.q: Macy's computer runs a face-recognition (machine learning) program faster than school computers. Possible reasons? (1) number of ports on the motherboard (2) number of cores (3) number of clock cycles per second
ex.a: (1) ports only decide how many peripherals can connect; not a performance factor. (2) more cores, more instructions executed in a given time. (3) is the clock rate; higher usually means faster. Answer: (2) and (3) only (Textbook Example 2.2 Q2).
ex.az: 連接埠數目與效能無關；核心數和時鐘頻率有關。

cards.en:
Word length (word size) is the number of bits processed by a CPU each time. It is the smallest unit of data stored in a computer (as described in the textbook). Nowadays it is usually 32 bits or 64 bits. A CPU with a longer word length usually performs better, but the relationship with processing speed is not linearly proportional.
Registers are usually 32 or 64 bits depending on word length, and bus width usually equals word length.
Reducing the word length means the CPU can address fewer memory locations (it must be the result), while effects on speed, clock rate or energy are not guaranteed.
cards.zh:
Word length（字長）/ word size = CPU 每次處理的位元數，課本說是電腦儲存資料的最小單位。現在通常是 32 或 64 bits。字長越長通常效能越好，但不成線性正比。
暫存器大小、bus width 通常與字長相同。
縮短字長必定令 CPU 可定址的記憶體位置減少；對速度、時鐘頻率、耗電則不一定。

ex.q: Which must be the result of reducing the word length of a CPU? A. energy consumption increased B. clock rate reduced C. processing speed increased D. number of memory locations the CPU can address is reduced
ex.a: Fewer bits per address means fewer addressable locations. Answer: D (Checkpoint 2.2 Q2).
ex.az: 答案 D。

ex.q: How many different addresses can a 32-bit address represent?
ex.a: 2<sup>32</sup> = 4 294 967 296 addresses (about 4 GB if each address holds 1 byte). With 64 bits: 2<sup>64</sup>.
ex.az: 2³² 個位址，約 4 GB。

cards.t: Misconception: 64-bit is not twice as efficient as 32-bit
cards.tz: 誤解：64 位元不是 32 位元的兩倍效率
cards.en:
Wrong: 'A 64-bit processor is twice as efficient as a 32-bit processor.'
Correct: The advantage of a 64-bit processor over a 32-bit processor is that it can address more memory and handle more complex functions. However, the relationship between word length and performance is not linearly proportional.
The same 'not linearly proportional' idea applies to clock rate and number of cores: doubling them does not double performance, because other components (RAM, storage speed) and the nature of the task also limit speed.
cards.zh:
錯誤：64-bit 處理器的效率是 32-bit 的兩倍。
正確：64-bit 的優點是可以定址更多記憶體（address more memory）及處理更複雜的功能；但字長與效能的關係不是線性正比。
同樣道理適用於時鐘頻率和核心數：加倍不等於效能加倍，因為 RAM、儲存速度和工作性質也會限制速度。

ex.q: A student says: 'My 8-core 4 GHz CPU is exactly twice as fast as a 4-core 4 GHz CPU.' Comment.
ex.a: Incorrect. More cores help multitasking, but the relationship between the number of cores and processing speed is not linearly proportional: some tasks must run in sequence, and RAM/storage speed may limit the CPU.
ex.az: 不正確，核心數與速度不成線性正比。

cards.en:
Random access memory (RAM) is volatile: data disappears once the computer shuts down. It stores data temporarily for processing, so the storage size and data access rate of RAM greatly affect the performance of a CPU. RAM's data access rate is lower than the CPU cache but higher than secondary storage.
RAM can easily be increased by adding or replacing RAM sticks on the motherboard. But check the motherboard design: versions such as DDR3, DDR4 and DDR5 SDRAM differ in shape and may not fit the slots of certain motherboards.
Why can frequently updated processing data not be kept in ROM? Because ROM cannot be rewritten.
cards.zh:
RAM（隨機存取記憶體）是 volatile，關機後資料消失，用來暫時儲存待處理資料，所以 RAM 的容量和存取速度大大影響 CPU 表現。速度比 CPU cache 慢，但比輔助儲存器快。
可以加裝或更換 RAM 條來增加 RAM，但要留意主機板設計：DDR3、DDR4、DDR5 SDRAM 形狀不同，未必插得入某些主機板的插槽。
為何經常更新的資料不能放 ROM？因為 ROM 不能改寫。

ex.q: Ryan replaces 8 GB DDR3 1066 MHz RAM with 16 GB DDR4 1600 MHz RAM but fails. Most likely reason?
ex.a: The new RAM must fit the motherboard slot, which depends on the RAM version. The motherboard does not support DDR4 RAM (Textbook Example 2.3 Q1, answer C). ROM is irrelevant.
ex.az: 主機板不支援 DDR4。

ex.q: Which about RAM is/are correct? (1) access rate higher than secondary storage (2) access rate higher than CPU cache (3) data disappears at shutdown
ex.a: (1) true, (2) false (cache is faster), (3) true. (1) and (3) only (Checkpoint 2.3 Q1, answer C).

cards.tz: 唯讀記憶體 ROM 與 BIOS
cards.en:
Read-only memory (ROM) is non-volatile: data persists after shutdown. Its data is expected to be read-only and usually cannot be rewritten.
A computer's ROM stores firmware (startup program), a collection of instructions required to start a computer. This firmware is called the basic input/output system (BIOS). The BIOS setup screen offers options such as standard CMOS features, boot settings, passwords.
Peripheral devices like printers and scanners also have RAM and ROM, but their RAM is smaller and the firmware in their ROM is not BIOS; it is the device's own firmware that controls its operation.
Since ROM is only used when booting, ROM size barely affects computer performance.
cards.zh:
ROM（唯讀記憶體）是 non-volatile，關機後資料仍在，通常不能改寫。
電腦的 ROM 存放 firmware（韌體 / 開機程式），即啟動電腦所需的指令，稱為 BIOS（基本輸入輸出系統）。
打印機、掃描器等周邊設備也有 RAM 和 ROM，但 RAM 較小，ROM 內的韌體不是 BIOS，而是控制該設備運作的韌體。
ROM 只在開機時使用，所以 ROM 容量幾乎不影響電腦效能。

ex.q: What is stored in the ROM of a scanner?
ex.a: Suggested answer: the scanner's firmware, i.e. the instructions needed to start up and control the scanner's operation (not BIOS) (Checkpoint 2.3 Q2).
ex.az: 掃描器的韌體（啟動及控制掃描器的指令）。

ex.q: Grace, a graphics designer, upgrades her desktop. Which greatly affect performance? (1) RAM size (2) ROM size (3) CPU clock cycle (4) weight
ex.a: RAM stores data for processing: yes. ROM only stores BIOS used at boot: no. Clock cycle sets clock rate: yes. Weight: no. (1) and (3) only (Textbook Example 2.4 Q2, answer B).
ex.az: RAM 容量和時鐘周期影響效能。

cards.tz: ROM 的種類及 UEFI（增潤）
cards.en:
Three types of ROM based on rewritability:
  • Programmable ROM (PROM): once programmed, its content cannot be rewritten.
  • Erasable programmable ROM (EPROM): content can be erased by exposure to ultraviolet light of certain intensity.
  • Electrically erasable programmable ROM (EEPROM): content can be erased by electricity.
Unified extensible firmware interface (UEFI) is a newer alternative firmware to BIOS; it may perform better than BIOS.
So 'ROM usually cannot be rewritten', but EPROM/EEPROM can be erased with special methods (this is how BIOS updates are possible on EEPROM/flash).
cards.zh:
按可改寫性，ROM 有三種：PROM：寫入後不能改寫；EPROM：用一定強度的紫外光照射可以擦除；EEPROM：可以用電擦除。
UEFI（統一可延伸韌體介面）是 BIOS 的較新替代韌體，效能可能較好。
所以 ROM「通常」不能改寫，但 EPROM/EEPROM 可用特別方法擦除（例如更新 BIOS）。

ex.q: Match: (i) erased by UV light (ii) erased electrically (iii) written once only.
ex.a: (i) EPROM (ii) EEPROM (iii) PROM.
ex.az: 紫外光 EPROM；電 EEPROM；一次 PROM。

cards.tz: 存取方法：順序存取與直接存取
cards.en:
Secondary storage uses two access methods:
  • Sequential access: data is written sequentially from the beginning; to access specific data the system searches through the storage sequentially, e.g. reaching the 5th element only after processing all elements before it. Device using sequential access only: magnetic tape. Its access rate varies depending on where the data is located and on average is lower than direct access.
  • Direct access (random access): data can be written in any position; each position has a unique address, so data is accessed directly without searching other positions. Devices: hard disk, USB flash drive, optical disks, floppy disk, SSD. Its access rate is more stable and generally higher.
Misconception: devices that use direct access can also use sequential access.
cards.zh:
Sequential access（順序存取）：資料由頭開始順序寫入；要讀某資料必須順序搜尋，例如讀第 5 個要先經過前 4 個。只能順序存取的設備：磁帶（magnetic tape）。速度視資料位置而變，平均較慢。
Direct access（直接存取，又稱 random access）：資料可寫在任何位置，每個位置有唯一位址，可直接讀取。設備：硬碟、USB 手指、光碟、軟碟、SSD。速度較穩定，一般較快。
誤解：直接存取的設備不能順序存取 ✗。正確：直接存取設備也可以順序存取。

ex.q: Which support(s) direct access? (1) hard disk (2) SSD (3) floppy disk
ex.a: All three use unique addresses. (1), (2) and (3) (Chapter Exercise MC 5, answer D).
ex.az: 三者都支援直接存取。

ex.q: Data records #1–#6 are stored. Compare how #5 is reached on a tape and on a hard disk.
ex.a: Tape (sequential): read past #1–#4 first (tape winding), then #5. Hard disk (direct): heads move straight to #5's unique address.
ex.az: 磁帶要經過 #1–#4；硬碟直接到 #5 的位址。

cards.t: Magnetic storage: magnetic tape and hard disk
cards.en:
Three common types of secondary storage by medium: magnetic, solid-state and optical.
Magnetic tape: a strip of plastic film coated with magnetic materials. Storage size large enough to be measured in TB (1 TB = 240 bytes); low unit price per capacity. But limited to sequential access, so low data access rate due to time consumed by tape winding. Therefore used for backup storage, not daily data. Prone to damage if kept in a humid environment.
Hard disk: many read/write heads and circular metal disks coated with magnetic material. Heads move directly to the unique addresses of data, so higher access rate than tape (direct access). Heads do not touch the disks, but may crash the metal disks on impact, so a hard disk is slightly less durable and portable than tape. Avoid moving the hard disk when the computer is on.
cards.zh:
輔助儲存器按媒體分：磁性、固態、光學。
Magnetic tape（磁帶）：塗上磁性物料的塑膠膜，容量以 TB 計（1 TB = 2⁴⁰ bytes），每單位容量價格低；但只可順序存取，要捲帶，所以存取慢，常用作備份（backup）而非日常資料。潮濕環境下易損壞。
Hard disk（硬碟）：有多個讀寫頭和塗磁性物料的金屬碟。讀寫頭直接移到資料位址（直接存取），所以比磁帶快。讀寫頭不接觸碟面，但撞擊時可能刮傷碟片，所以比磁帶較不耐用和不便攜。開機時避免移動硬碟。

ex.q: Ben backs up 500 GB of videos to a hard disk instead of an SSD. Possible reason? A. unit price per capacity of hard disks is usually lower B. hard disks are shock resistant C. access rates of hard disks are higher D. hard disks are non-volatile
ex.a: B false (prone to damage on impact), C false (SSD faster), D true but SSDs are non-volatile too, so it is not a reason to prefer a hard disk. Answer: A (Chapter Exercise MC 4).
ex.az: 硬碟每單位容量較便宜，答案 A。

cards.t: Solid-state storage: SSD, memory card, USB flash drive
cards.tz: 固態儲存：SSD、記憶卡、USB 手指
cards.en:
Solid-state drive (SSD): flash memory plus a controller (reads and writes data). Flash memory is a storage medium that can be read and written electrically at a fast speed. An SSD has no moving parts, so it is more durable and portable than tape and hard disk and consumes less energy; but it has a higher unit price per capacity.
Memory card: flash memory, designed to be small for mobile devices (digital cameras, smartphones). Secure Digital (SD) is a common format in different sizes (SD, microSD with adapter).
USB flash drive: flash memory + integrated USB interface (often USB-A). Small and easy to use; used for backup and data transfer between devices.
Three advantages of SSD over hard disk: higher data access rate, more durable (no moving parts), lower energy consumption (also lighter/more portable).
cards.zh:
SSD（固態硬碟）：快閃記憶體（flash memory）+ 控制器。快閃記憶體可以用電高速讀寫。SSD 沒有活動部件，所以比磁帶和硬碟更耐用、更便攜、更省電，但每單位容量價格較高。
Memory card（記憶卡）：快閃記憶體，體積細小，用於相機、手機；常見格式 SD（另有 microSD）。
USB flash drive（USB 手指）：快閃記憶體 + USB 介面（多為 USB-A），細小易用，用於備份和在設備之間傳送資料。
SSD 比硬碟的三個優點：存取較快、較耐用（無活動部件）、較省電（亦較輕便）。

ex.q: Give three advantages of using an SSD over a hard disk.
ex.a: Suggested answer: (1) higher data access rate; (2) more durable, no moving parts, so not damaged by impact; (3) lower energy consumption; (also more portable) (Checkpoint 2.4 Q2).
ex.az: 較快、較耐用、較省電。

ex.q: Paul carries about 12 GB of files between home and office and edits them often. Floppy disk, magnetic tape, CD-ROM or USB flash memory?
ex.a: Floppy: too small. Tape: drive uncommon at home, sequential. CD-ROM: cannot be rewritten. USB flash memory: usually >12 GB, no extra drive needed, small and easy to carry (Example 2.4 Q1, answer D).
ex.az: USB 手指：容量夠、可改寫、易攜帶。

cards.en:
An optical disk is a circular plastic disk coated with a reflective material. Data is represented by grooves on the plastic and read by laser beams from an optical drive. Scratches may divert the laser and corrupt data.
TypeStorage size
Compact disc (CD)usually 700 MB
Digital versatile disc (DVD)usually 4.7 GB
Blu-ray disc (BD)usually 25 GB to 128 GB
RewritabilityType
Cannot be written and rewrittenCD-ROM, DVD-ROM, BD-ROM
Written once onlyCD-R, DVD-R, BD-R
Can be rewrittenCD-RW, DVD-RW, BD-RE
cards.zh:
Optical disk（光碟）是塗上反光物料的圓形塑膠碟，資料以碟面的坑紋（grooves）表示，由光碟機的激光讀取。刮花會令激光偏離而損壞資料。
容量：CD 約 700 MB；DVD 約 4.7 GB；BD 約 25–128 GB。
可寫性：-ROM 不能寫入（CD-ROM、DVD-ROM、BD-ROM）；-R 只能寫一次（CD-R、DVD-R、BD-R）；-RW / -RE 可重寫（CD-RW、DVD-RW、BD-RE）。

ex.q: A 20 GB video project must be archived once on a single disc and never changed. Which disc type?
ex.a: CD (700 MB) and DVD (4.7 GB) are too small; choose a BD-R (25 GB+, write once).
ex.az: 20 GB 要用 BD，只寫一次用 BD-R。

ex.q: How many full CDs are needed to store 4 GB (take 1 GB = 1024 MB)?
ex.az: 需要 6 張 CD。

cards.en:
AttributeMagnetic tapeHard diskSSDOptical disk
Storage mediaMagneticMagneticFlash memoryOptical
Storage sizeVery largeLargeMediumSmall
Unit price per capacityLowLowHighLow to medium
Access methodSequentialDirectDirectDirect
Data access rateUnstable and lowestMediumHighMedium
DurabilityProne to damage if kept in a humid environmentProne to damage on impactDurableProne to damage when scratched
Use this table to justify device choices in structured questions: large cheap backup → tape/hard disk; speed and durability → SSD; distribution of read-only media → optical disk.
cards.zh:
背熟此表：
磁帶：磁性、容量極大、單價低、順序存取、速度不穩定且最慢、潮濕易損。
硬碟：磁性、容量大、單價低、直接存取、速度中等、撞擊易損。
SSD：快閃記憶體、容量中、單價高、直接存取、速度高、耐用。
光碟：光學、容量小、單價低至中、直接存取、速度中、刮花易損。
答結構題時用來解釋選擇：大量平價備份 → 磁帶/硬碟；速度和耐用 → SSD；分發唯讀資料 → 光碟。

ex.q: A bank must keep 200 TB of transaction logs for 7 years and rarely reads them. Recommend a device with two reasons.
ex.a: Magnetic tape: (1) very large storage size; (2) lowest unit price per capacity. Its slow sequential access does not matter because the data is rarely read (backup). Keep it away from humidity.
ex.az: 磁帶：容量極大、單價最低，少讀取所以慢也無妨。

cards.en:
A redundant array of independent disks (RAID) consists of multiple storage devices, such as hard disks and SSDs, for:
  • improvement in data transfer rate;
  • error detection;
  • reducing the chance of data loss due to device failure.
RAID is not a must in a system unit; it is used mostly in servers and NAS.
cards.zh:
RAID（冗餘磁碟組）由多個儲存設備（如硬碟、SSD）組成，目的：
  • 提高資料傳輸速度；
  • 錯誤偵測；
  • 減少因設備故障而遺失資料的機會。
RAID 不是主機必須的組件，多用於伺服器和 NAS。

ex.q: A school server stores students' work on four hard disks combined as a RAID. Give two benefits.
ex.a: (1) If one disk fails, data can still be recovered, reducing the chance of data loss due to device failure; (2) higher data transfer rate (also error detection).
ex.az: 減少因硬碟故障遺失資料；提高傳輸速度。

cards.t: Network storage: NAS and cloud storage
cards.tz: 網絡儲存：NAS 與雲端儲存
cards.en:
Network-attached storage (NAS) is a file server with many drives combined into a RAID. It allows users on a local area network (LAN) to read and write at the same time.
Cloud storage is a service often provided by Internet service providers (ISP). With an Internet connection, users can read and write data anytime and anywhere (e.g. Google Drive in a browser). However, users may need to pay regularly, especially for large storage sizes.
Compare: NAS works within the LAN, owned by the organisation, one-off cost; cloud storage needs Internet, accessible anywhere, recurring fee.
cards.zh:
NAS（網絡儲存設備）是一部把多個硬碟組成 RAID 的檔案伺服器，讓區域網絡（LAN）內的用戶同時讀寫。
Cloud storage（雲端儲存）通常由 ISP 等提供，只要有互聯網連線就可以隨時隨地讀寫（例如用瀏覽器開 Google Drive）；但可能要定期付費，尤其容量大時。
比較：NAS 在 LAN 內使用、機構自己擁有、一次性成本；雲端要上網、隨處可用、要持續付費。

ex.q: A design studio wants all 10 staff in the office to share large project files at the same time, without monthly fees. NAS or cloud storage?
ex.a: NAS: staff on the LAN can read and write at the same time; data is protected by RAID; no regular storage fee (cloud storage needs payment for large sizes and depends on the Internet connection).
ex.az: NAS：LAN 內同時讀寫，有 RAID，不用月費。

cards.en:
Storage can be arranged into a hierarchy based on data access rate, storage size and unit price per capacity. The higher the storage is located, the higher its data access rate, the smaller its storage size and the higher its unit price per capacity.
From top to bottom:
  1. Register
  2. Cache memory in a processor
  3. RAM (main memory)
  4. SSD (secondary storage)
  5. Hard disk (secondary storage)
  6. Magnetic tape (secondary storage)
Top: highest access rate, smallest size, highest unit price. Bottom: lowest access rate, largest size, lowest unit price.
cards.zh:
儲存設備可按存取速度、容量、每單位容量價格排成層級。位置越高：存取越快、容量越小、單價越高。
由上至下：Register → Cache memory → RAM（主記憶體）→ SSD → Hard disk → Magnetic tape。
最上：最快、最小、最貴；最下：最慢、最大、最便宜。

ex.q: Which has the highest data access rate? A. Register B. RAM C. SSD D. Cache memory
ex.a: Register is at the top of the hierarchy. Answer: A (Chapter Exercise MC 9).
ex.az: 暫存器最快。

cards.en:
AttributeDesktopLaptopTablet
Screen sizeNo embedded monitor; potentially large (placed on a table)MediumSmall
PortabilityLow: needs many peripherals, heavyMedium: moderate size and weightHigh: small, light
Computing powerHighMediumLow
Storage sizeLargeMediumSmall
Embedded devicesNoneMonitor, keyboard, touchpad, speakers, microphone, webcamMonitor, touchscreen, speakers, microphone, camera
Nowadays most smartphones, smart TVs and game consoles can function as computers (virtual keyboards, Internet browsing). Smartwatches and smartglasses are rarely seen but are computers too.
A tablet usually consumes less energy than a desktop because of lower computing power and a smaller screen.
cards.zh:
按大小：
桌上電腦：沒有內置顯示器但可接大螢幕；便攜性低（要多個周邊、重）；運算能力高；容量大；沒有內置設備。
手提電腦：中等螢幕、中等便攜、運算中、容量中；內置顯示器、鍵盤、觸控板、喇叭、咪、網絡攝影機。
平板電腦：螢幕小、便攜性高（細、輕）、運算低、容量小；內置顯示器、觸控屏、喇叭、咪、相機。
現在智能手機、智能電視、遊戲機都可當電腦；智能手錶、智能眼鏡也是電腦。平板因運算能力低、螢幕小，通常比桌上電腦省電。

ex.q: Advantages of a tablet over a desktop for watching videos? (1) more portable (2) larger screen (3) higher computing power (4) lower energy consumption
ex.a: Tablet: light with built-in monitor, so more portable; usually smaller screen; lower computing power; lower energy consumption. (1) and (4) only (Example 2.5 Q1, answer B).

ex.q: Marvin, a college student, must carry his computer to classes and mainly writes essays. Desktop, laptop or tablet? Justify.
ex.a: Suggested answer: a laptop: medium portability with a built-in keyboard and monitor for typing essays; enough computing power and storage for coursework. (A desktop is not portable; a tablet lacks a physical keyboard and has low storage.)
ex.az: 手提電腦：便攜，又有鍵盤方便寫文章。

cards.en:
Activity 2.1 compares models by type, price, screen size, resolution, CPU (clock rate and number of cores), memory (RAM size, e.g. 16 GB DDR4; tablets use embedded RAM), storage (HDD/SSD/embedded) and weight.
Method:
  1. Identify the main task (word processing, video editing, VR, mobility).
  2. Performance factors: CPU clock rate, number of cores, RAM size, GPU type (dedicated vs integrated), SSD vs HDD.
  3. Non-performance factors: weight/portability, screen size, price. The number of ports does not affect performance; ROM size barely affects it.
  4. Justify with 2 points linked to the scenario.
cards.zh:
課本活動 2.1 比較不同型號：類型、價錢、螢幕、解像度、CPU（時鐘頻率、核心數）、記憶體（RAM 大小，平板用內置 RAM）、儲存（HDD/SSD/內置）、重量。
方法：
  1. 找出主要用途。
  2. 效能因素：CPU 時鐘頻率、核心數、RAM 容量、GPU 類型、SSD vs HDD。
  3. 非效能因素：重量/便攜、螢幕、價錢。連接埠數目不影響效能；ROM 容量幾乎不影響。
  4. 用兩點配合情境解釋。

ex.q: Mr. Chan compares a laptop (3.6 GHz, 16 GB RAM, discrete GPU, 1 TB, 4 USB, 2.4 kg) and a tablet (2 GHz, 4 GB, integrated GPU, 128 GB, 1 USB, 0.8 kg). (a) Two reasons to use the laptop for a VR application. (b) Two reasons to use the tablet for participants to experience AR.
ex.a: (a) Suggested answer: discrete GPU gives higher graphics processing power for rendering VR; higher CPU clock rate (3.6 GHz) and larger RAM (16 GB) process data faster (also larger storage for VR content). (b) Suggested answer: lighter (0.8 kg) / more portable, participants can move it around to view AR; it has a built-in camera and touchscreen needed for AR (also lower cost per device) (Chapter Exercise Long Q1).
ex.az: (a) 獨立 GPU、較高時鐘頻率和較大 RAM。(b) 輕便、有內置相機和觸控屏。

cards.en:
HardwareDevelopment
CPUHigher computing power (higher clock rate, more cores); higher energy efficiency
Storage deviceLarger storage size; higher data access rate; smaller physical size (e.g. small external SSD); longer lifespan; higher energy efficiency
Display unit (monitor, projector)Higher resolution and pixel density; higher frame rate; more choices of screen sizes; 3D vision without glasses; portable and foldable (e.g. foldable smartphone); higher energy efficiency
Microphone, speaker, earphoneHigher sound quality (higher sampling rate, higher bit depth); higher energy efficiency
GPU trend: higher graphics processing power. Note the common theme: higher energy efficiency everywhere, so 'higher power usage', 'higher operating temperature' or 'smaller RAM' are not trends. For smartphones the focus is e.g. higher resolution and higher computational power, not more USB ports.
cards.zh:
硬件發展趨勢：
CPU：運算能力更高（時鐘頻率更高、核心更多）；能源效率更高。
儲存設備：容量更大、存取更快、體積更小（如細小外置 SSD）、壽命更長、更節能。
顯示設備：解像度和像素密度更高、幀率更高、更多尺寸選擇、裸眼 3D、可攜和可摺疊（如摺機）、更節能。
咪、喇叭、耳機：音質更高（取樣率更高、位元深度更高）、更節能。
GPU 趨勢：圖形處理能力更高。共同點是更節能，所以「耗電更高、溫度更高、RAM 更小」都不是趨勢。智能手機重點：解像度、運算能力，不是更多 USB 埠。

ex.q: Which is a trend of GPU development? A. higher power usage B. higher operation temperature C. smaller RAM size D. higher graphics processing power
ex.a: Answer: D (Chapter Exercise MC 10).
ex.az: 答案 D。

ex.q: Main focus of smartphone technology development? (1) higher resolution (2) higher computational power (3) more USB ports
ex.a: (1) and (2) only (Checkpoint 2.5 Q1, answer A).

mc.q:
Which of the following components must be found in a system unit?
(1) RAM
(2) Hard disk
(3) Dedicated graphics card
mc.e: RAM is essential; an SSD can replace a hard disk; an iGPU can replace a graphics card.

cards.tz: 计算机系统：硬件与软件
cards.en:
A computer system consists of hardware and software. Hardware is the physical parts of the computer (e.g. CPU, monitor, keyboard, RAM). Software is the data or instructions designed to help the computer accomplish specific tasks. Hardware alone cannot do anything useful: it needs software to tell it what to do. Software alone cannot run: it needs hardware to execute on.
Software is divided into two types: system software and application software. A quick test: if the program mainly exists to control the machine and support other programs, it is system software; if it exists to let a user do a specific job (write an essay, edit a photo), it is application software. In the exam, always classify using the textbook wording.
cards.zh:
计算机系统 = 硬件 (hardware) + 软件 (software)。硬件是看得见摸得着的物理部件，例如 CPU、显示器、键盘、RAM；软件是 the data or instructions designed to help the computer accomplish specific tasks，即让电脑完成特定工作的数据或指令。两者缺一不可：硬件没有软件什么都做不了，软件没有硬件也无法运行。
软件分为两大类：system software（系统软件） 和 application software（应用软件）。判断方法：主要用来控制机器、为其他程序提供平台的是系统软件；让用户完成某项具体工作（写文章、修图）的是应用软件。考试时尽量用课本的英文定义作答。

ex.q: Classify each as hardware or software: (i) RAM module (ii) Microsoft Excel (iii) printer driver (iv) touchscreen.
ex.a:
(i) hardware: physical part.
(ii) software: application software.
(iii) software: a driver program (system software).
(iv) hardware: physical input/output device.
ex.az: RAM 和触屏是物理部件→硬件；Excel 和驱动程序是指令→软件（Excel 是应用软件，驱动是系统软件）。

cards.tz: 系统软件与应用软件比较
cards.en:
Table 3.1 compares the two types:
AttributeSystem softwareApplication software
ExampleMicrosoft Windows, macOSMicrosoft Excel, Adobe Photoshop
UsageControls the hardware operationAllows users to perform specific tasks
DependenceManages system resources and provides a platform for application softwareRuns on a platform provided by system software
Programming languageUsually written in low-level languagesUsually written in high-level languages
Key point: application software cannot run without system software, but system software does not depend on any particular application. System software includes the operating system, utility programs and driver programs (Section 3.2).
cards.zh:
课本 Table 3.1 从四方面比较：
• 例子：系统软件如 Windows、macOS；应用软件如 Excel、Photoshop。
• 用途：系统软件 controls the hardware operation；应用软件 allows users to perform specific tasks。
• 依赖关系：系统软件 manages system resources and provides a platform for application software；应用软件 runs on a platform provided by system software。
• 编程语言：系统软件通常用 low-level languages 写（要直接控制硬件、追求效率）；应用软件通常用 high-level languages。
重点：应用软件离不开系统软件，反之不然。系统软件包括 operating system、utility programs、driver programs。

ex.q: Is it possible to generate a bar chart for a spreadsheet file using system software only? Explain briefly. (Checkpoint 3.1 Q1)
ex.a: No. Generating a bar chart is a specific task for the user, which is done by application software (e.g. spreadsheet software such as Microsoft Excel). System software only controls the hardware operation and provides a platform for application software.
ex.az: 不行。画柱状图是用户的特定任务，要用应用软件（如 Excel）；系统软件只负责控制硬件和提供平台。

cards.t: Relationship among users, software and hardware
cards.tz: 用户、软件与硬件的关系
cards.en:
Fig. 3.1 shows a layered relationship:
User --uses--> Application software (e.g. Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop) --runs on a platform provided by--> System software (e.g. Microsoft Windows, macOS) --controls--> Hardware (e.g. CPU, monitor).
Memorise the three verbs: the user uses application software; application software runs on a platform provided by system software; system software controls hardware. The user normally never talks to hardware directly. When you print from Word, Word asks the OS, the OS uses the printer's driver program, and the driver controls the printer. Exam diagrams often blank out one box ("What is X?"), so learn the order.
cards.zh:
Fig. 3.1 是分层关系：
User → uses → Application software → runs on a platform provided by → System software → controls → Hardware。
要背三个动词：用户 uses 应用软件；应用软件 runs on a platform provided by 系统软件；系统软件 controls 硬件。用户一般不直接操作硬件。例如在 Word 按打印：Word 请求 OS，OS 通过打印机驱动程序，驱动再控制打印机。考试常把其中一格挖空问“X 是什么”，所以要记清顺序。

ex.q: A diagram shows: User → (controls) → Application programs → (run on) → X. What is X?
ex.a: X is system software, because application software runs on a platform provided by system software. (Not a driver program, cache or main memory.)
ex.az: X 是系统软件，因为应用程序运行在系统软件提供的平台上。

cards.en:
An operating system (OS) controls the hardware operation and interacts with driver programs and application software. It is the most important piece of system software: it starts when the computer boots, stays in memory, and acts as the middle layer between applications and hardware. Examples: Microsoft Windows, Apple macOS, Android, iOS, Linux.
Its functions (Table 3.2) fall into: resources management (process, memory, peripheral device, file system and disk management), user interface, user management and multitasking. Note that features such as database management belong to a DBMS, and checking for viruses belongs to a utility program (virus checker); these are not necessarily OS functions.
cards.zh:
Operating system (OS) controls the hardware operation and interacts with driver programs and application software. OS 是最重要的系统软件：开机即加载，常驻内存，是应用程序和硬件之间的中间层。例子：Windows、macOS、Android、iOS、Linux。
功能（Table 3.2）分四类：resources management（process、memory、peripheral device、file system、disk management）、user interface、user management、multitasking。注意：database management 是 DBMS 的功能；检查病毒 是 virus checker（实用程序）的功能，都不一定是 OS 的功能，常作 MC 陷阱。

ex.q: Which of the following is NOT a primary function of an OS? A. Provide the user interface B. Manage the memory C. Manage the file system D. Check for viruses in the system
ex.a: D. Checking for viruses is done by a virus checker, which is a utility program, not a primary function of the OS.
ex.az: D：查毒是实用程序 virus checker 的工作。

cards.en:
Resources management functions of an OS (Table 3.2):
  • Process management: arranges processes for the CPU to execute or cancels processes.
  • Memory management: allocates the memory of RAM for processing.
  • Peripheral device management: controls the input and output of peripheral devices via driver programs.
  • File system management: builds a file system to organise folders and files.
  • Disk management: controls how files are stored physically in the secondary storage. Formatting erases all data in secondary storage and configures it for initial use. Partitioning divides the secondary storage into more than one part so that different parts can be managed individually.
Tip: file system management is the logical view (folders/files); disk management is the physical view (where bits are stored, format, partition).
cards.zh:
OS 的资源管理功能：
  • Process management：安排进程给 CPU 执行，或取消进程。
  • Memory management：为处理分配 RAM。
  • Peripheral device management：通过 driver programs 控制外围设备的输入输出。
  • File system management：建立文件系统来组织文件夹和文件。
  • Disk management：控制文件在辅助存储器上如何物理存放。Formatting（格式化）会清除全部数据并配置为初始可用状态；Partitioning（分区）把辅助存储器分为多个部分，各自独立管理。
区分：file system management 是逻辑层（文件夹、文件）；disk management 是物理层（格式化、分区、实际存放位置）。

ex.q: Match each action to an OS function: (i) a hung program is closed; (ii) a new hard disk is split into C: and D:; (iii) a USB printer starts printing a document.
ex.a:
(i) Process management (cancel a process).
(ii) Disk management: partitioning.
(iii) Peripheral device management via the printer's driver program.
ex.az: (i) 进程管理；(ii) 磁盘管理中的分区；(iii) 通过驱动程序的外围设备管理。

cards.t: OS functions: user interface, user management, multitasking
cards.tz: OS 功能：用户界面、用户管理、多任务
cards.en:
The other OS functions in Table 3.2:
  • User interface: presents information on a screen and allows users to interact with the computer. It may be a GUI or a CLI.
  • User management: allows users to create user accounts and provides security; allows the administrator to manage the account settings, such as passwords and access rights.
  • Multitasking: running more than one task (program) at the same time. Most operating systems nowadays support multitasking, e.g. playing music while editing a document.
Exam point: the user interface is an OS function, but a GUI specifically is not necessarily a feature, because some OS support CLI instead of GUI (Example 3.1 Q1).
cards.zh:
Table 3.2 其余功能：
  • User interface：在屏幕显示信息并让用户与电脑互动，可以是 GUI 或 CLI。
  • User management：让用户建立账户并提供保安；让管理员管理账户设定，如密码和 access rights。
  • Multitasking：同时运行多个任务，如边听音乐边打文件；现今大多数 OS 都支持。
考点：“提供用户界面”是 OS 功能，但“图形用户界面 GUI”不一定是，因为有些 OS 只用 CLI（Example 3.1 Q1）。

ex.q: Which of the following is not necessarily a feature of an OS? (1) Peripheral device management (2) GUI (3) Memory management (4) Database management
ex.a: (2) and (4). Some OS provide a CLI instead of a GUI; database management is a feature of a DBMS, not necessarily of an OS. Answer: (2) and (4) only. (Example 3.1 Q1, answer D)
ex.az: (2)(4)：有的 OS 只有 CLI；数据库管理属于 DBMS。

cards.tz: 单用户与多用户操作系统
cards.en:
Based on the number of users allowed to access the OS at the same time (Table 3.3):
  • Single-user OS: allows only one user to access the operating system at the same time. It may have more than one user account, but only one person uses it at a time (e.g. a family PC with Windows 11 accounts for each member).
  • Multi-user OS: allows more than one user to access the operating system at the same time, and arranges system resources, like CPU time and storage space, for different users (e.g. a Linux server many users log into remotely; Windows Server).
Misconception: "many accounts = multi-user". Wrong: the test is simultaneous access.
cards.zh:
按 同一时间可访问的用户数 分（Table 3.3）：
  • Single-user OS：同一时间只允许一个用户使用；可以有多个用户账户（如家用 Windows 11 每人一个账户），但同一时间只有一人用。
  • Multi-user OS：允许多个用户同时访问，并为不同用户分配 CPU time 和 storage space 等资源（如多人远程登录的 Linux 服务器、Windows Server）。
误区：“有多个账户就是多用户 OS”是错的，关键是 同时。

ex.q: A home PC running Windows 11 has 4 user accounts for each family member. Is it a multi-user OS?
ex.a: No. Windows 11 is a single-user OS: although it has more than one user account, it allows only one user to access it at the same time.
ex.az: 不是。虽有多个账户，但同一时间只有一人使用，属单用户 OS。

cards.tz: 桌面、移动与网络操作系统
cards.en:
Based on the purpose (Table 3.4):
  • Desktop OS (e.g. Microsoft Windows): used for desktop and laptop computers; more comprehensive due to high hardware and software compatibility; mostly single-user.
  • Mobile OS (e.g. iOS): used for handheld mobile devices like tablets, smartphones and smartwatches; more hardware optimisations, such as disabling applications from running in the background and screen timeout, for prolonging the battery life; mostly single-user.
  • Network OS (e.g. Linux): used for servers that allow multiple computers to connect and communicate; provides services like file sharing, web hosting and database management; mostly multi-user.
cards.zh:
按 用途 分（Table 3.4）：
  • Desktop OS（如 Windows）：用于台式机和笔记本；因硬件和软件兼容性高而 more comprehensive；多为单用户。
  • Mobile OS（如 iOS）：用于平板、手机、智能手表；有更多硬件优化，例如 禁止应用在后台运行、屏幕超时熄灭，以 prolong the battery life；多为单用户。
  • Network OS（如 Linux）：用于让多台电脑连接和通讯的服务器，提供 file sharing、web hosting、database management 服务；多为多用户。

ex.q: Why does a mobile OS stop apps running in the background when the screen is off?
ex.a: It is a hardware optimisation of a mobile OS for prolonging the battery life: background apps use CPU, memory and network, which drain the battery of a handheld device.
ex.az: 这是移动 OS 为延长电池寿命做的优化，后台应用会耗电。

cards.tz: 图形用户界面与命令行界面
cards.en:
Based on the user interface (Table 3.5):
Graphical user interface (GUI): interact via graphical elements such as windows, icons, menus and buttons; presents information as multimedia (text, images); more intuitive and easy to use for new users; usually involves keyboards and pointing devices (mice, touchscreens).
Command line interface (CLI): interact via a specific list of text commands; usually text output; requires fewer system resources, such as memory, and usually runs faster than GUI due to the lack of graphics; high flexibility and efficiency for experienced users; requires users to learn text commands; keyboard only, no pointing devices.
Choose GUI for beginners; CLI for experts, servers and repetitive bulk jobs.
cards.zh:
按 用户界面 分（Table 3.5）：
GUI：通过 windows, icons, menus and buttons 等图形元素操作；可用文字、图像等多媒体显示；more intuitive and easy to use for new users；通常用键盘加 pointing devices（鼠标、触屏）。
CLI：输入 text commands 操作；多以文字显示；requires fewer system resources (e.g. memory) and usually runs faster than GUI due to the lack of graphics；对熟手 high flexibility and efficiency；但要学命令；只用键盘，不用指点设备。
新手选 GUI；专家、服务器、大量重复工作选 CLI。

ex.q: Thomas only started learning computers recently. OS A uses a GUI and OS B uses a CLI. Suggest one reason for him to install OS A.
ex.a: A GUI is more intuitive and easier to use for new users: he can use a mouse to click icons and menus instead of having to learn and memorise text commands.
ex.az: GUI 对新手更直观，用鼠标点图标即可，不必记命令。

cards.t: Using the CLI: cd, copy and the * wildcard
cards.tz: CLI 实操：cd、copy 与通配符 *
cards.en:
Activity 3.2 shows the power of the CLI. Combining 99 txt files by opening each and copy-pasting in a GUI is tedious. In Windows Command Prompt (Start → type cmd → Command Prompt):
cd C:\Users\Public\text
copy *.txt combine.txt
cd [path] means changing directory. copy [source file] [target file] copies the content of the source file to the target file. * is a wildcard, so *.txt means all txt files in the current folder; copying many sources into one target concatenates them. One line replaces 99 manual copy-and-paste operations, which illustrates the high flexibility and efficiency of CLI for experienced users.
cards.zh:
Activity 3.2：用 GUI 逐个打开 99 个 txt 再复制粘贴非常繁琐。在 Windows 命令提示符（开始 → 输入 cmd）：
cd C:\Users\Public\text
copy *.txt combine.txt
cd = change directory（切换目录）；copy [source] [target] 把来源文件内容复制到目标文件；* 是 wildcard（通配符），*.txt 表示当前文件夹所有 txt 文件，多个来源复制到一个目标就会合并。一条命令代替 99 次手工操作，体现 CLI 对熟手 flexible and efficient。

ex.q: Write the commands to combine all .txt files in D:\notes into a file all.txt.
ex.a:
cd D:\notes
copy *.txt all.txt
(If the current drive is not D:, type D: first or use cd /d D:\notes.)
ex.az: 先 cd 到文件夹，再 copy *.txt all.txt。

cards.en:
Table 3.6:
OSPurposeInterfaceDeveloped by
Microsoft WindowsMostly desktop OSMainly GUIMicrosoft
Apple macOSDesktop OSMainly GUIApple
AndroidMobile OSMainly GUIOpen source, based on Linux
iOSMobile OSMainly GUIApple
LinuxMostly network OSSupports CLI, may support GUIOpen source
Traps: Linux does support GUI in some distributions (Debian, Fedora, Ubuntu). iOS is not open source: it is developed and owned by Apple. Common Windows like Windows 10/11 are single-user, but Windows Server, as a network OS, is multi-user.
cards.zh:
Table 3.6 要背：Windows（多为桌面 OS、主要 GUI、Microsoft）；macOS（桌面、GUI、Apple）；Android（移动、GUI、开源、基于 Linux）；iOS（移动、GUI、Apple）；Linux（多为网络 OS、支持 CLI，也可能支持 GUI、开源）。
陷阱：Linux 有 GUI（Debian、Fedora、Ubuntu 等发行版）；iOS 不是开源，由 Apple 拥有；Windows 10/11 是单用户，但 Windows Server 作为网络 OS 是多用户。

ex.q: Which is true? (1) Linux does not support GUI. (2) Windows Server, as a network OS, is a multi-user OS. (3) iOS is open source.
ex.a: (2) only. (1) is false: Debian, Fedora and Ubuntu support GUI. (3) is false: iOS is developed and owned by Apple. (Example 3.1 Q2, answer B)
ex.az: 只有 (2) 正确。

cards.en:
Utility programs (utility software) are programs that maintain a computer system and improve its efficiency. They usually come with an operating system, and there are also third-party utility programs that can be installed selectively. They are system software, because they look after the computer itself rather than doing a user's job.
The textbook's list (Table 3.7): file manager, system monitor, virus checker, firewall software, data compressor, defragmentation software, backup software, uninstaller. Utility programs are also used for virtualisation (e.g. Oracle VM VirtualBox).
Trap: a word processor is not a utility program; it is productivity (application) software.
cards.zh:
Utility programs（实用程序）are programs that maintain a computer system and improve its efficiency. 通常随 OS 附带，也有可选择安装的第三方实用程序。属于系统软件，因为它们照顾电脑本身，而不是做用户的具体工作。
课本列表（Table 3.7）：file manager、system monitor、virus checker、firewall software、data compressor、defragmentation software、backup software、uninstaller。虚拟化也靠实用程序（如 VirtualBox）。
陷阱：word processor 不是实用程序，是生产力（应用）软件。

ex.q: Which are utility programs? (1) System monitor (2) Virus checker (3) Data compressor (4) Word processor
ex.a: (1), (2) and (3) only. A word processor is productivity software (application software).
ex.az: (1)(2)(3)，文字处理器是应用软件。

cards.tz: 文件管理器与系统监察软件
cards.en:
File manager (e.g. Finder in macOS, File Explorer in Windows): can show, add, copy or delete files in a file system. It is the user's window into the OS file system.
System monitor (e.g. Task Manager in Microsoft Windows, Activity Monitor in macOS): monitors the running processes and shows system resource usage, like CPU usage, memory usage and network traffic. For example, it can show current processes, kill processes that are not responding, and disable programs from running on startup.
Typical exam use: a computer is slow or a program has frozen → open the system monitor, find the process using high CPU/memory and end it, or stop unneeded startup programs so booting is faster.
cards.zh:
File manager（文件管理器）（如 macOS Finder）：show, add, copy or delete files in a file system。
System monitor（系统监察软件）（如 Windows 工作管理员 Task Manager）：monitors the running processes and shows system resource usage, like CPU usage, memory usage and network traffic；例如显示当前进程、kill 无响应的进程、禁止程序开机自动启动。
考试常见情境：电脑变慢或程序卡死 → 用 system monitor 找出占用大量 CPU/内存的进程并结束，或关闭不需要的开机启动程序。

ex.q: A game freezes and cannot be closed by its own window. Which utility helps and how?
ex.a: A system monitor (e.g. Task Manager). It shows the running processes; the user selects the not-responding game process and kills (ends) it.
ex.az: 用 system monitor（如工作管理员）找到无响应进程并结束。

cards.tz: 病毒侦测程序与防火墙软件
cards.en:
Virus checker (e.g. Avast Antivirus): also known as anti-virus software or anti-malware. It checks for computer viruses and removes them. It needs to be updated constantly so that it has the latest information to judge whether a file or program is a virus or not. An outdated virus checker may miss new viruses.
Firewall software (e.g. Firewall in macOS): monitors network traffic and protects computers against viruses from the network, by allowing or blocking connections.
Difference: a virus checker scans files/programs already on (or arriving at) the computer; a firewall watches the network traffic going in and out. They complement each other.
cards.zh:
Virus checker（病毒侦测程序）（如 Avast）：又称 anti-virus software / anti-malware；checks for computer viruses and removes them；必须 updated constantly 才有最新资料判断文件或程序是否是病毒，过时的病毒库会漏掉新病毒。
Firewall software（防火墙软件）（如 macOS 防火墙）：monitors network traffic and protects computers against viruses from the network，允许或阻挡连接。
分别：virus checker 扫描电脑上的文件/程序；firewall 监察进出的网络流量。两者互补。

ex.q: Mary's virus checker failed to detect a new virus released last week. Give a likely reason.
ex.a: Her virus checker was not updated, so it did not have the latest information (virus definitions) to judge that the new program was a virus.
ex.az: 病毒库没有更新，缺少最新资料。

cards.en:
A data compressor (e.g. 7zip) can compress, decompress and manage the compressed files. Examples of compressed formats: zip, rar and 7z.
Benefits of compressing multiple files into a single file:
  • Data can be transmitted easily with smaller file size and a smaller number of files.
  • The folder structure is maintained and can be restored once decompressed.
  • Compressed files can be password protected.
Limitation: files that are already compressed, such as JPG photos, MP3 or MP4, shrink very little when zipped again, because the redundancy has already been removed.
cards.zh:
Data compressor（数据压缩程序）（如 7zip）：compress, decompress and manage the compressed files；格式例子 zip、rar、7z。
把多个文件压缩成一个文件的好处：
  • 文件更小、数量更少，方便传送；
  • 保留文件夹结构，解压后可还原；
  • 可加密码保护。
限制：JPG、MP3、MP4 等 本身已压缩 的文件再压缩几乎不会变小，因为冗余数据已被去掉。

ex.q: Rex's travel photos are saved as JPG. Zipping them barely saves space. Why?
ex.a: JPG is already a compressed format, so little redundant data remains; a data compressor cannot reduce the size much further.
ex.az: JPG 已经是压缩格式，再压缩效果很小。

cards.t: Defragmentation software, backup software and uninstaller
cards.tz: 磁碟重组、备份软件与解除安装程序
cards.en:
Defragmentation software (e.g. Microsoft Drive Optimizer): computer storage becomes fragmented upon long time usage; fragmented storage results in low data access rate and inefficient usage; defragmentation software redistributes the location of files in storage to improve the data access rate and storage efficiency.
Backup software (e.g. Time Machine in macOS): creates a backup of files and system settings; in case of data corruption or computer system malfunction, the system can be restored to the previous state using the backup.
Uninstaller (e.g. Programs and Features in Windows): shows most of the software installed in a computer and uninstalls specific ones, freeing storage space.
cards.zh:
Defragmentation software（磁碟重组软件）：长期使用后存储会 fragmented，导致 data access rate 低、使用效率差；重组软件 redistributes the location of files 以提高读取速度和存储效率。
Backup software（备份软件）（如 Time Machine）：备份文件及系统设定；数据损坏或系统故障时可 restore to the previous state。
Uninstaller（解除安装程序）：显示已安装的软件并删除指定软件，释放空间。

ex.q: Tommy must not lose his important work files. Suggest a utility program and explain its use.
ex.a: Backup software. It creates a backup (copy) of his files and system settings regularly; if the files are corrupted or the computer malfunctions, he can restore the files to the previous state from the backup.
ex.az: 备份软件：定期备份，出问题时还原。

cards.en:
Fragmentation occurs when many files are created, edited and deleted when the file system is used for a long time. Files are stored in blocks. When a file grows but the next block is taken by another file, the extra part must be stored elsewhere, so the file is split into separate fragments. When a file is deleted, it leaves a gap; a new larger file fills the gap and spills over to later blocks.
In Table 3.8: A(4) and B(3) and C(5) are created in order; A grows to 6 (2 blocks placed after C); B is deleted leaving a 3-block hole; D(6) fills the hole and continues after A; A grows to 9. Result: files A and D are stored as separate fragments, and such separation reduces the efficiency of data access (the read head on an HDD must jump between places).
cards.zh:
Fragmentation occurs when many files are created, edited and deleted when the file system is used for a long time. 文件按块存放。文件变大但后面的块已被占用，多出的部分只能放到别处，于是被分成 separate fragments；删除文件会留下空洞，新的较大文件填空洞后再溢出到后面。
Table 3.8：依次建立 A(4)、B(3)、C(5)；A 增至 6（多出的 2 块放在 C 后）；删除 B 留下 3 格空位；D(6) 先填空位再接到后面；A 再增至 9。结果 A 和 D 被分成多段，降低数据读取效率（硬盘磁头要来回跳）。

ex.q: Storage has 8 blocks per row. A(3) is created, then B(2), then A grows to 5. How many fragments does A have?
ex.a: A uses blocks 1-3; B uses 4-5; A's 2 extra blocks go to 6-7. A is in 2 fragments (1-3 and 6-7), separated by B.
ex.az: A 被 B 隔开，共 2 段。

cards.en:
Defragmentation reorganises the data in storage to achieve a higher data access rate and more efficient usage. Therefore many operating systems regularly defragment their storage.
Table 3.9 steps: move a fragment of file D away to make room for A; regroup fragments of A until there is no more space or separated fragments; move file C to make room for A; regroup A; move C back; move a fragment of D to make room for itself; regroup D. Final result: each file occupies contiguous blocks.
Notes: defragmentation does not delete data and does not create free space; it only rearranges files (free space becomes contiguous). Think about: SSDs are believed not to need defragmentation because they have no moving read/write head, so access time is nearly the same wherever data is, and extra writes shorten SSD life.
cards.zh:
Defragmentation reorganises the data in storage to achieve a higher data access rate and more efficient usage. 很多 OS 会定期自动重组。
Table 3.9 过程：把 D 的一段移开给 A 腾位；重组 A；把 C 移开；再重组 A；C 移回；D 腾位给自己并重组。最后每个文件占 连续的块。
注意：重组 不删除数据、不增加可用空间，只是重新排列（空余空间变连续）。Think about：SSD 被认为不需要重组，因为 没有机械磁头，任何位置读取时间差不多，而且额外写入会缩短 SSD 寿命。

ex.q: Ken has 8 GB free and wants to install a 24 GB game. After running defragmentation there is still not enough space. Why? (Checkpoint 3.1 Q2)
ex.a: Defragmentation only rearranges the locations of files to improve access rate and storage efficiency; it does not delete data or increase the total free space. He still has about 8 GB free, less than 24 GB.
ex.az: 重组只重新排列文件，不会增加空闲空间。

cards.en:
Driver programs are used to control peripheral devices by translating requests into machine level commands. Each driver program is designed for a specific OS to control a specific peripheral device.
Fig. 3.2: the operating system uses driver programs A, B, C, which control the mouse, keyboard and speaker. Driver programs may support hot swapping, which allows us to plug or swap the devices when the computer system is still operating.
Ways to get drivers: some come with operating systems; some can be downloaded from the websites of the device manufacturers; some are stored on installation CDs or USB flash drives that come with the devices.
Misconception: "a mouse needs no driver". Wrong: basic devices still need drivers, which simply come with the OS and are installed automatically.
cards.zh:
Driver programs（驱动程序）are used to control peripheral devices by translating requests into machine level commands. Each driver program is designed for a specific OS to control a specific peripheral device.
Fig. 3.2：OS uses 驱动程序，驱动程序 controls 鼠标、键盘、喇叭。驱动可支持 hot swapping（热插拔）：电脑运行中插入或更换设备。
取得驱动的途径：随 OS 附带；从 设备制造商网站下载；设备附带的安装 CD 或 USB 手指。
误区：“鼠标不需要驱动”是错的，只是驱动随 OS 附带并自动安装。

ex.q: Herman can use his mouse without manually installing a driver. He believes a mouse does not need a driver program. Is he correct?
ex.a: No. Every peripheral device needs a driver program to translate requests into machine level commands. The mouse driver comes with the operating system and was installed automatically, so he did not need to install it manually.
ex.az: 不对。鼠标也需要驱动，只是随 OS 附带、自动安装。

ex.q: After replacing his GPU, Herman's new GPU does not function. Suggest a reason.
ex.a: The driver program for the new GPU has not been installed/updated (or the old driver is not compatible with the new GPU), so the OS cannot control the device.
ex.az: 没有安装新显卡的驱动程序。

cards.en:
Application software allows users to perform specific tasks and runs on a platform provided by system software. The book groups it into (but not limited to) four types:
  • Productivity software: produce, analyse or present information.
  • Communication software: exchange information between users via a network.
  • Media development software: create or edit multimedia files.
  • Educational software: acquire knowledge, enhance learning efficiency or assist teaching.
When asked which software a person needs, list the operating system too: every application needs one. E.g. an office assistant in an animation studio needs an OS, productivity software (documents) and communication software (email).
cards.zh:
应用软件让用户完成特定任务，运行于系统软件提供的平台上。课本分为（但不限于）四类：
  • Productivity software（生产力软件）：产生、分析或展示信息。
  • Communication software（通讯软件）：经网络在用户间交换信息。
  • Media development software（媒体开发软件）：建立或编辑多媒体文件。
  • Educational software（教育软件）：获取知识、提升学习效率或协助教学。
问“某人需要什么软件”时别忘了 OS，任何应用都需要它。

ex.q: Tommy is an office assistant in an animation studio. Which does he need? (1) OS (2) productivity software (3) communication software
ex.a: (1), (2) and (3). He needs an OS for any software to run, productivity software for documents and spreadsheets, and communication software such as email to contact others.
ex.az: 三者都需要。

cards.tz: 生产力软件与办公套件
cards.en:
Productivity software is used to improve the productivity of working. It is used to produce, analyse or present information. Table 3.10:
TypeFunctionExample
Word processorEdit document and apply text formatMicrosoft Word, OpenOffice Writer
Spreadsheet softwareEvaluate formulae and generate charts for data analysisMicrosoft Excel, OpenOffice Calc
Presentation softwareCreate slide shows for presentationsMicrosoft PowerPoint, OpenOffice Impress
Database management systemDefine and maintain databasesMicrosoft Access, OpenOffice Base
Different productivity software are often distributed as a bundle called an office suite. Applications in a suite share similar user interfaces and are designed to interact with each other, so data can be transferred between them with very little data loss (e.g. a Word table pasted into Excel keeps most formats).
cards.zh:
Productivity software is used to improve the productivity of working. It is used to produce, analyse or present information.
• Word processor：编辑文件、设定文字格式（Word、Writer）
• Spreadsheet：计算公式、生成图表作数据分析（Excel、Calc）
• Presentation：制作简报（PowerPoint、Impress）
• DBMS：定义和维护数据库（Access、Base）
Office suite（办公套件）：多种生产力软件打包发行；界面相似、设计上可互相配合，数据可以在它们之间转移且 very little data loss（如 Word 表格复制到 Excel 保留大部分格式）。

ex.q: Give two advantages of buying an office suite rather than separate programs from different vendors.
ex.a:
1. Applications share similar user interfaces, so users learn them faster.
2. They are designed to interact with each other, so data can be transferred between applications with very little data loss (e.g. a Word table copied into Excel keeps its formats).
ex.az: 界面相似易学；数据互传几乎不失真。

cards.en:
Communication software is used to exchange information between users via a network for communication purposes. Table 3.11:
TypeFunctionExample
Web browserBrowse and interact with the internetGoogle Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Safari
Email clientSend, receive and manage emailsMicrosoft Outlook, Mozilla Thunderbird
Messaging applicationSend, receive and manage real-time messagesWhatsApp, WeChat, Skype, Signal, Facebook Messenger
Web conferencing softwareHold live meetings which connect more than one party over the internet remotelyZoom, Google Meet
File sharing softwareTransfer and receive programs and multimedia via internetFileZilla, BitTorrent
Distinguish an email client (stored, not necessarily instant) from a messaging application (real-time).
cards.zh:
Communication software is used to exchange information between users via a network for communication purposes.
• Web browser：浏览互联网（Chrome、Firefox、Safari）
• Email client：收发、管理电邮（Outlook、Thunderbird）
• Messaging application：收发 实时 讯息（WhatsApp、WeChat、Signal）
• Web conferencing：经互联网举行多方实时会议（Zoom、Google Meet）
• File sharing：经互联网传送程序和多媒体（FileZilla、BitTorrent）
注意区分 email client（非实时）与 messaging app（实时）。

ex.q: A school holds a parents' meeting with 50 parents at home. Which type of communication software is most suitable? Give an example.
ex.a: Web conferencing software, e.g. Zoom or Google Meet: it holds a live meeting connecting more than one party over the internet remotely.
ex.az: Web conferencing 软件，如 Zoom。

cards.en:
Media development software is used to create or edit multimedia files. Table 3.12:
  • Image editing software: Paint.NET, Adobe Photoshop, Inkscape, Adobe Illustrator.
  • Audio editing software: Audacity, Adobe Audition.
  • Video editing software: Corel VideoStudio, Adobe Premiere.
Media development software is usually demanding on hardware (large files, heavy processing) and is normally run through a GUI, not a CLI, because users need to see and manipulate images, waveforms and timelines with pointing devices. Choose the type by the media: a podcast → audio editing; a school promo clip → video editing; a poster → image editing.
cards.zh:
Media development software is used to create or edit multimedia files.
• Image editing：Paint.NET、Photoshop、Inkscape、Illustrator
• Audio editing：Audacity、Adobe Audition
• Video editing：Corel VideoStudio、Adobe Premiere
这类软件通常对硬件要求高，并以 GUI 操作（需要用鼠标/触屏直接看和编辑图像、波形、时间线），不会用 CLI。按媒体选类型：播客→音频；宣传片→视频；海报→图像。

ex.q: Classify: Audacity, Adobe Premiere, Inkscape.
ex.a: Audacity: audio editing software. Adobe Premiere: video editing software. Inkscape: image editing software. All are media development software.
ex.az: 音频、视频、图像编辑软件。

cards.en:
