cards.zh:
Educational software is used to acquire knowledge, enhance learning efficiency or assist educational workers in teaching students.
• Encyclopaedia：概览各种主题（Wikipedia、Britannica）
• Dictionary：查词义（Oxford Dictionary of English）
• Scientific calculator：计算数学式解决科学问题（WolframAlpha、Microsoft Math Solver）
• Learning management system（LMS）：老师管理学生学习进度；学生学习和温习（Moodle、Edmodo、Google Classroom、Socrative）

ex.q: A teacher wants to post homework, collect submissions and track each student's progress. Which educational software type fits?
ex.a: A learning management system (e.g. Google Classroom, Moodle): it lets educational workers manage students' learning progress, and lets students learn and revise.
ex.az: 学习管理系统 LMS，如 Google Classroom。

cards.en:
Different computers have different modes of operation. These modes can be categorised by when to process and how to process.
  • When: batch processing (collect data, process later at regular intervals) vs real-time processing (process as soon as data is received).
  • How: parallel processing (multiple processors in one system, shared memory) vs distributed processing (multiple computers over a high-speed network, memory never shared).
  • Also: virtualisation, dividing hardware into virtual portions.
Exam technique: identify the clue words. "Immediately / up-to-date" → real-time; "at night / monthly / collected first" → batch; "processors" → parallel; "computers in a network" → distributed.
cards.zh:
不同电脑有不同 modes of operation（运作方式），按 when to process（何时处理） 和 how to process（如何处理） 分类：
  • 何时：batch（先收集、定时处理）vs real-time（收到即处理）。
  • 如何：parallel（同一系统多处理器、共享内存）vs distributed（经高速网络的多台电脑，内存从不共享）。
  • 另有 virtualisation（虚拟化）。
答题技巧：找关键词——“即时/最新”→实时；“晚上/每月/先收集”→成批；“处理器”→并行；“网络中多台电脑”→分布式。

ex.q: Classify: (i) payroll run on the last day of each month; (ii) an online multiplayer game; (iii) a render farm of 100 networked PCs.
ex.a: (i) Batch processing. (ii) Real-time processing. (iii) Distributed processing.
ex.az: (i) 成批 (ii) 实时 (iii) 分布式。

cards.en:
A batch processing system collects data without immediately processing it. Instead, data is processed in a batch at regular intervals.
Advantages:
  • Makes good use of idling system resources as the processes can be scheduled overnight;
  • Processes a large volume of similar data in one go;
  • Relatively less expensive to operate and set up as immediate responses are not required.
Examples: a bank producing monthly statements and performing autopay in non-peak hours (early morning); scheduled data backup; academic transcript printing.
Disadvantage: results are not up-to-date between runs. Batch is unsuitable when the user needs an immediate response (e.g. booking a seat).
cards.zh:
A batch processing system collects data without immediately processing it. Instead, data is processed in a batch at regular intervals.
优点：
  • 可安排在夜间，善用闲置资源；
  • 一次处理大量同类数据；
  • 不需即时回应，运作和建置成本较低。
例子：银行 月结单、非繁忙时段（清晨）的 autopay；定时备份；打印成绩表。
缺点：两次处理之间数据不是最新的，不适合需要即时回应的情况。

ex.q: Tommy receives many emails and replies to them all each morning. Batch or real-time? Explain.
ex.a: Batch processing. He collects the emails without processing them immediately, and processes (replies to) them together in a batch at a regular interval (every morning).
ex.az: 成批处理：先收集，每天早上一次处理。

cards.en:
A real-time processing system processes data as soon as the data is received. It allows users to get immediate responses that are up-to-date. However, it requires large computing power and main memory to keep its response time short.
Examples: a bank's ATM transactions; self-driving systems; restaurant booking systems; online gaming; navigation apps showing current location and traffic.
Choosing: if two users could act on the same data (e.g. the same cinema seat), the system must update immediately to prevent double booking, so real-time is required. Compare with the postman example (Checkpoint 3.2): letters collected at 6 o'clock then delivered is closer to batch, because the letters are collected first and handled together at a regular time.
cards.zh:
A real-time processing system processes data as soon as the data is received. It allows users to get immediate responses that are up-to-date. 但 requires large computing power and main memory to keep its response time short。
例子：银行 ATM、自动驾驶、餐厅订座、网络游戏、显示实时位置和路况的导航应用。
选择：多人可能同时争同一数据（如同一戏院座位），必须即时更新防止重复订票，所以要实时。对比 Checkpoint 3.2 邮差例子：信件先收集、6 点统一处理，较接近 batch。

ex.q: Cindy builds an online ticket system for her cinema. Batch or real-time? Explain. (Checkpoint 3.2 Q1)
ex.a: Real-time processing. Seat availability must be updated as soon as a ticket is sold, so customers get immediate, up-to-date responses and the same seat is not sold twice.
ex.az: 实时处理：座位要即时更新，避免重复售票。

cards.en:
A parallel processing system usually consists of multiple processors and memory can be shared among these processors. The system may:
  • assign a task for each processor so that multiple tasks are performed concurrently to achieve multitasking (Task A→Processor 1, B→2, C→3); or
  • divide a task into multiple portions and assign a portion for each processor so that every portion is performed concurrently and the task can be accomplished in a shorter time (Subtasks X, Y, Z).
Limitation: some tasks are like relay races: though divisible, the portions have to be performed in a certain order, so they cannot benefit from parallel processing.
Example: an online shop allocating different transactions to different processors.
cards.zh:
A parallel processing system usually consists of multiple processors and memory can be shared among these processors. 可以：
  • 每个处理器负责一个任务，同时执行多个任务以实现 multitasking；或
  • 把一个任务分成多部分，每个处理器做一部分，同时进行，缩短完成时间。
限制：有些任务像 接力赛（relay races），虽可分拆但必须按顺序进行，无法受惠于并行处理。
例：网购平台把不同交易分配给不同处理器。

ex.q: A task has 4 independent parts each taking 10 s on one processor. Estimate the time on 1 processor and on 4 processors. What if each part needs the previous part's result?
ex.a: 1 processor: 4 × 10 = 40 s. 4 processors in parallel: about 10 s (ignoring overhead). If each part depends on the previous one (like a relay race), they must run in order: still about 40 s, so no benefit.
ex.az: 独立时约 10 秒；有先后依赖时仍要 40 秒。

cards.en:
A distributed processing system consists of a high-speed network and multiple computers. A program or a computer is used to manage the interaction between these computers.
It has high scalability, as the number of computers in the system can be increased or decreased according to our needs. Like parallel processing, it can achieve multitasking and improve performance; the difference is that tasks or subtasks are performed by different computers instead of different processors. Unlike parallel processing, memory is never shared. Because the computers communicate over a network, network connectivity is a must.
Example: a film studio using many computers in a network to render visual effects: faster rendering, and more computers can be added when needed.
cards.zh:
A distributed processing system consists of a high-speed network and multiple computers. A program or a computer is used to manage the interaction between these computers.
High scalability：电脑数量可按需增减。与并行处理一样可 achieve multitasking and improve performance；不同之处是由 不同电脑（而非不同处理器）执行任务，而且 memory is never shared。必须有网络连接。
例：电影公司用网络中多台电脑渲染特效：速度更快，且可按需加电脑。

ex.q: A film studio uses multiple computers in a network for rendering. (a) Which processing? (b) Two advantages.
ex.a:
(a) Distributed processing.
(b) 1. Rendering is divided among computers and done concurrently, so it finishes in a shorter time (better performance).
2. High scalability: computers can be added or removed according to needs.
ex.az: (a) 分布式 (b) 更快完成；可扩展性高。

cards.tz: 并行处理与分布式处理比较
cards.en:
Parallel processingDistributed processing
HardwareMultiple processors (usually in one system)Multiple computers + high-speed network
MemoryCan be shared among processorsNever shared
ManagementWithin the systemA program or a computer manages the interaction
Network needed?NoYes, must
Common pointsBoth can assign different tasks (multitasking) or subtasks of one task to different units to run concurrently and improve performance
Trap (Example 3.2): "Parallel processing can divide a task into subtasks and assign them to different computers" is false: that is distributed processing.
cards.zh:
比较：
• 硬件：parallel 是多个 处理器；distributed 是多台 电脑 + 高速网络。
• 内存：parallel 可共享；distributed 从不共享。
• 管理：distributed 由一个程序或一台电脑管理各电脑的互动。
• 网络：distributed 必须有网络。
• 共同点：都可把不同任务或同一任务的子任务分给不同单位同时执行以提升效能。
陷阱（Example 3.2）：“并行处理把子任务分给不同 电脑”是 错 的，那是分布式。

ex.q: Which are correct? (1) Distributed processing requires network connectivity. (2) Batch processing does not process data once the data is received. (3) Parallel processing can divide a task into subtasks and assign them to different computers.
ex.a: (1) and (2) only. (3) is wrong: parallel processing assigns tasks to different processors, not computers. (Example 3.2 Q1, answer A)

cards.en:
Virtualisation divides the computer hardware into multiple virtual portions with the help of utility programs. For example, a portion of system resources (computing power, main memory, secondary storage) can be assigned to create a virtual machine (VM), which functions as an independent computer, so that:
  • it may run an operating system different from the original computer; and
  • it can install software that is not compatible with the operating system of the original computer.
Therefore virtualisation increases the flexibility of computers and saves the cost of buying actual hardware devices. Common utility programs: Oracle VM VirtualBox, Windows Virtual PC.
To create a VM to run software for another OS, you need a utility program (to create the VM) and the other OS; no extra application software is required.
cards.zh:
Virtualisation divides the computer hardware into multiple virtual portions with the help of utility programs. 例如分出部分 CPU 运算能力、主存、辅助存储来建立 virtual machine（虚拟机），它像一部独立电脑：
  • 可运行 与原电脑不同的 OS；
  • 可安装 与原电脑 OS 不兼容的软件。
因此虚拟化 增加电脑的灵活性并节省购买实体硬件的成本。常用实用程序：Oracle VM VirtualBox、Windows Virtual PC。
要用 VM 运行别的 OS 的软件：需要 utility program（建立 VM）和 那个 OS，不需要额外应用软件。

ex.q: Owen wants a virtual machine on his computer to play mobile games. Excluding the games, which does he need? (1) Application software (2) Operating system (3) Utility program
ex.a: (2) and (3) only. A utility program (e.g. VirtualBox) divides the hardware to create the VM, then a mobile OS is installed on it. No other application software is needed. (Example 3.2 Q2, answer C)
ex.az: 需要 OS 和实用程序。

sq.q: Thomas has just started to learn about using computers and is choosing between OS A (interface: GUI) and OS B (interface: CLI).

parts.q: Suggest one reason for Thomas to install OS A.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: GUI is more intuitive / easier to use for new users; he can click icons/menus with a mouse instead of learning text commands.

parts.q: Thomas installs OS A. He wants to install an application that only supports OS C. Suggest a method for him.
parts.ms: Create a virtual machine (using a utility such as VirtualBox) and install OS C on it, then install the application in the VM.

sq.src: Textbook B Ch3 Chapter Exercise LQ1 (p.116)

sq.q: Herman has been using his current computer for a long time.

parts.q: The access rate of his hard disk is becoming slower. Suggest a method and explain how it boosts access speed without buying a new storage device.
parts.ms:
Run defragmentation software.
It redistributes/regroups the fragments of files so each file is stored contiguously, improving the data access rate.

parts.q: He replaces his GPU with a more powerful one, but after installing it the GPU does not function. Suggest a possible reason.
parts.ms: The driver program of the new GPU is not installed / not compatible / not updated.

parts.q: He can use his mouse without manually installing a driver, so he believes a mouse does not need a driver program. Is he correct? Explain.
parts.ms:
No.
The mouse still needs a driver program; it comes with the operating system and is installed automatically.

sq.src: Textbook B Ch3 Chapter Exercise LQ2 (p.116)

sq.q: Rex took many photos while travelling and saved them as jpg.

parts.q: He does not have enough storage space and uses a data compressor, but it does not help much. Why?
parts.ms: JPG is already a compressed format, so further compression reduces size very little.

parts.q: Suggest two methods for Rex to organise the images.
parts.ms: Any two: use a file manager to create folders (e.g. by date/place) and move photos into them; rename files meaningfully; compress each trip's folder into one archive (keeps folder structure); back up / move to external storage or cloud; delete unwanted duplicates.

sq.src: Textbook B Ch3 Chapter Exercise LQ3 (p.117)

sq.q: Tommy receives many emails every day. He replies to the emails each morning.

parts.q: Which mode of operation, batch or real-time processing, best describes his action? Explain.
parts.ms:
Batch processing.
Emails are collected without being processed immediately and are processed together at a regular interval (each morning).

parts.q: He stores many important work files. Suggest a utility program to avoid losing them and explain its use.
parts.ms:
Backup software.
It creates backups of files (and system settings) so that they can be restored after data corruption or system malfunction.

sq.src: Textbook B Ch3 Chapter Exercise LQ4 (p.117)

sq.q: A film studio uses multiple computers in a network to render visual effects.

parts.q: Which kind of processing does this belong to?
parts.ms: Distributed processing.

parts.q: Suggest two advantages of this processing method.
parts.ms:
Tasks/subtasks are performed concurrently by many computers, so rendering finishes in a shorter time / better performance.
High scalability: computers can be added or removed according to needs.

sq.src: Textbook B Ch3 Chapter Exercise LQ5 (p.117)

sq.q: Answer the following.

parts.q: Cindy wants to create an online ticket system for her cinema. Suggest batch or real-time processing and explain.
parts.ms:
Real-time processing.
Seat availability must be updated as soon as a ticket is sold, giving customers up-to-date responses and avoiding selling the same seat twice.

parts.q: People put letters into a post-box. At 6 o'clock a postman collects all letters and immediately delivers them. Which mode, batch or real-time, is closer? Explain.
parts.ms:
Batch processing.
Letters are collected over the day without being handled immediately, then processed together at a regular time (6 o'clock).

sq.q: Answer the following.

parts.q: Is it possible to generate a bar chart for a spreadsheet file using system software? Explain.
parts.ms:
No.
Generating a chart is a specific user task performed by application software (spreadsheet software); system software only controls hardware and provides a platform.

parts.q: Ken has 8 GB free and wants to install a 24 GB game. After defragmentation there is still not enough space. Why?
parts.ms:
Defragmentation only rearranges the location of files to improve access rate/efficiency.
It does not delete data or increase total free space, which is still about 8 GB < 24 GB.

sq.q: A school IT technician manages a Linux server that 200 students log into at the same time to save their coursework. The technician uses a CLI to manage it.

parts.q: Is the server's OS a single-user or multi-user OS? Give one reason.
parts.ms:
Multi-user OS.
More than one user accesses the OS at the same time; it arranges resources like CPU time and storage space for different users.

parts.q: Based on purpose, which type of OS is it? State one service it provides.
parts.ms:
Network OS.
File sharing / web hosting / database management.

parts.q: Give two reasons why the technician may prefer a CLI.
parts.ms:
Requires fewer system resources (e.g. memory) and runs faster due to lack of graphics.
High flexibility and efficiency for experienced users, e.g. one command with wildcards processes many files.

parts.q: Name the OS function that lets the technician set each student's password and access rights.
parts.ms: User management.

sq.q: Mr Chan's office computer has become slow and sometimes infected.

parts.q: Name the utility program he can use to find which running process uses most CPU and memory, and state one other thing it can do.
parts.ms:
System monitor (e.g. Task Manager).
Kill not-responding processes / disable programs from running on startup / show network traffic.

parts.q: His virus checker did not detect a newly released virus. Give a reason and a remedy.
parts.ms:
The virus checker was not updated, so it lacked the latest information.
Update it constantly/regularly.

parts.q: State how firewall software differs from a virus checker.
parts.ms:
Firewall monitors network traffic and protects against threats from the network.
A virus checker checks files/programs for viruses and removes them.

parts.q: Name a utility that removes software he no longer needs.
parts.ms: Uninstaller.

sq.q: A university runs a large simulation. Option 1: one server with 64 processors sharing memory. Option 2: 64 separate computers connected by a high-speed network.

parts.q: Name the mode of operation of each option.
parts.ms:
Option 1: parallel processing.
Option 2: distributed processing.

parts.q: State one difference between the two in terms of memory.
parts.ms: Parallel: memory can be shared among processors; distributed: memory is never shared.

parts.q: Give one advantage of Option 2.
parts.ms: High scalability: computers can be added/removed according to needs.

parts.q: Some parts of the simulation must be run one after another. Explain why these parts cannot benefit from either option.
parts.ms:
The parts depend on each other and must be performed in a certain order (like a relay race).
So they cannot run concurrently on different processors/computers.

sq.q: A secondary school is setting up computers for teachers and students.

parts.q: Name the type of application software and one example for: (i) making slide shows; (ii) defining and maintaining student records; (iii) managing students' learning progress.
parts.ms:
(i) Presentation software, e.g. Microsoft PowerPoint.
(ii) Database management system, e.g. Microsoft Access.
(iii) Learning management system, e.g. Google Classroom / Moodle.

parts.q: Give two advantages of installing an office suite.
parts.ms:
Applications share similar user interfaces.
Data can be transferred between applications with very little data loss.

parts.q: The school's video club edits promotional videos. Which category of application software is needed? Give an example.
parts.ms: Media development software (video editing), e.g. Adobe Premiere / Corel VideoStudio.
